## 20.52 WHY STATICS KEEP FAILING ON SCHEMA QUESTIONS: OUR DUMP STORES ONLY 7%
## OF .data. THE BLOB IS READABLE, THE RESOLVER IS NOT - AND THAT IS A PROPERTY
## OF THE DUMP, NOT OF THE SCHEMA. (2026-08-25 ~18:00)

Lane M closed with "statics cannot produce the entry bytes - three lanes have
converged on that." The conclusion is right and the reason is more specific,
which matters because the stated reason ("the schema objects are runtime-built")
implies nothing offline can ever work, while the real one names a fixable gap.

### Verified from the PE headers of RE_output/destiny2_unpacked_full.exe

| section | VSize | RawSize stored | |
|---|---|---|---|
| .text | 28,898,816 | 28,898,816 | FULL |
| .rdata | 3,667,968 | 3,667,968 | FULL |
| **.data** | **23,849,392** | **1,746,432** | **TRUNCATED - 7%** |
| .pdata / .vmp0 / .tls / .rsrc / .reloc / .idata / .text(2) | - | - | FULL |

Every section is complete EXCEPT `.data`, which stores 1,746,432 of 23,849,392
bytes. Anything past offset 1,746,432 into `.data` is simply absent from the
file, and reads there return nothing - which is what `pe_reader.off()` reports
as unmapped.

Where the schema globals fall:

  - `DAT_141f44e20` (schema blob)      offset   212,512 -> **READABLE**
  - `DAT_142439c70` (resolver global)  offset 5,409,904 -> NOT IN FILE
  - `DAT_142742fb0` (W1 live-read)     offset 8,593,328 -> NOT IN FILE

So the two globals every schema lane has needed are past the cut, while the blob
they derive from is fully present, as is all of `.rdata` and `.text`.

### What this changes

Not Lane M's route - the live read stays valid. What it changes is the SHAPE of
the problem: this is a dump-coverage gap, not an unknowable. A full-memory dump
of a running client would contain the resolver global, the runtime-built nodes
and their 0x28-byte entries, and it would be a PERMANENT artifact - every future
schema question answered offline instead of costing a boot each.

`comsvcs.dll` is present on the rig (verified), so the built-in path needs no
install:

    rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump <pid> <out.dmp> full

Also worth naming: **our client DLL is already inside the process.** Reading
`module_base + 0x2439c70` and walking from it is a memory read, not a function
detour - simpler and lower-risk than hooking 0x1404c72e0's entry, IF the type-12
node can be located without capturing the packed key. If the key is genuinely
needed, the hook stands.

### A tension in the leading hypothesis, recorded so it is not lost

Lane M section 6.3 proposes that our post-epoch bits are being consumed as
`peer_and_player_counts`, causing rejection before any row is parsed. That fits
key_only == full_mirror exactly.

But the SOLO body has the same post-epoch layout - root, revision, epoch, then
the slot-0 presence bit and the local row - and it is accepted and acknowledged.
If those bits were being misread as a counts field, the solo body should
misalign too. The lane covers this with "single-player tolerance or a different
schema path (W1 OPEN #3's two dialects)", which is the weakest link in an
otherwise well-cited chain.

The live read settles it either way, so this is not a blocker - but if the
transcribed entry list shows no counts field ahead of the member table, that
hypothesis dies and the divergence is elsewhere. Do not let the hypothesis
survive a read that refutes it.

## 20.51 THE APPLIED ROW DRIVES NOTHING. THE CLIENT ACKS A PEER-BEARING BODY,
## TOUCHES NO STEAM SURFACE, AND NEITHER GUARDIAN IS VISIBLE. THE ROW SHAPE IS
## ANSWERED AND CLOSED; THE PRIME SUSPECT IS NOW A COUNT FIELD.
## (2026-08-25 ~17:43, follow-up to 20.50)

### The discriminator 20.50 asked for

Both players stood in the Tower, at the shared spawn, for the whole window.
NEITHER SAW THE OTHER. The user's words: "we spawn in the same place so i
would've definitely seen it."

That alone proves less than it looks - 20.38 established that visibility is
peer-AUTHORED, so a roster entry could be correct and still show nobody until
the peer link forms. What closes the gap is the client's own networking trace.

### Verified by execution

Mac client, whole run: **13 `ev=steamnet` lines total**, all sign-in scaffolding
- `interface_acquired`, `identity`, `get_certificate`, `relay_ticket_count`,
two `lobby_create`, seven `stub`. **Zero `send_rendezvous`, ever.** And after
the peer bodies landed at t=230910: **zero ev=steamnet lines of any kind.**

So the client acknowledged a body carrying a remote member row and then touched
no Steam surface at all. Applying the membership row triggers NOTHING.

This weakens 20.44's reframe substantially. "Retail clients do not self-start
joins from search results; the SERVER declares membership and the client then
contacts the peer" - we declared it, the client accepted it, and no contact
followed. The declaration is evidently not the trigger, or not sufficient.

### The row shape is closed

`key_only` and `full_mirror` produced identical client behaviour because THE
ROW WAS NEVER READ. memberKey alone is sufficient to be accepted (20.50) and no
field addition changes anything. Shape was never the variable. Do not sweep it
again.

### The prime suspect, and why it fits everything

Lane M's field registry (RE_output/claims/msg12-parser-read.md 1b) names the
parsed structure:

  session_id, update_number, incremental_setup, **peer_and_player_counts**,
  peer_updates, player_updates, player_seq_number, leader_peer_index,
  host_peer_index, slot_counts, party nonce, checksum

with the lane's own note: *"a SEPARATE peer_and_player_counts field exists
upstream of them - our body does not currently distinguish counts from
valid-masks."*

Our encoder (activity_replicate_membership_encoder.cpp:12,28,35-36) writes
`masks = 0b11` twice - the two valid-masks - and nothing that is plainly a
count.

Hypothesis: the count still says one member, so the client parses our slot-1
row into a slot it then ignores. This fits EVERY observation at once - the body
parses, the revision acks, the peer never appears, the shape is irrelevant, and
no connection is attempted because there is no peer to connect to.

Corroboration that the row does reach the client: the Mac's type-12 receipts
grow 3891 -> 3976 bytes when the peer row is present, +85 bytes against
kPeerRowExtraBits = 673 bits (84.125 B, byte-padded to 85). The bits ship and
parse; they are simply not counted.

### Second lead, from the same lane

The peer-link failure-reason enum, ~44 entries at .rdata 0x141c9e2f8 - the
client's own vocabulary for why a peer add failed (`not-joinable`,
`no-reservation`, `address-invalid`, `player-count-zero`, `session-full`, ...).
Three parallel registries, no direct code xrefs (double indirection), flagged
by Lane M as a follow-up. Surfacing which reason fires would have the client
name our cause outright instead of us inferring it.

### Next

Both leads are disassembly, in the lane that was paused for this sweep. Resume
it with this boot's evidence added: ack succeeds, zero Steam surface activity
afterwards, no visual. That is information the lane did not have, and it points
at the count rather than the row.

## 20.50 THE SHAPE WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM - THE REVISION WAS. BOTH SESSIONS
## ACKNOWLEDGE A PEER-BEARING BODY, AND memberKey ALONE IS ENOUGH.
## (2026-08-25 ~17:38, server exe 427766a2456f493a, opencode paused)

The sweep, fixed to give each shape its own revision (p2(41)), walked for the
first time. Both sessions then applied a body carrying a remote member row.

### Verified by execution

Sweep progression (server log, both sessions interleaved):

  session A 0xB34F7851304A19CF: key_only x4 -> `membership_sweep result=retired
    variant=key_only next=key_account` at t=470966 -> key_account x3, last at
    t=477745
  session B 0x846C8338F7D022E6: key_only x3, last at t=477326

Both stop there. The log runs on to t=579647 - ~100 s - with BOTH clients
connected (232 and 250 frames, two key fingerprints) and `membership=1` on all
48 subsequent keepalives, so neither `hasMembership` nor the connection ended
the loop. Revisions during the window: 4 -> 5 (peer gained, opencode's p2(39))
-> 6 (the sweep's retire republish).

  - **Session A acknowledged revision 6, which carried `key_account`.**
  - **Session B acknowledged revision 5, which carried `key_only`.**

### What this settles

The bisect premise was wrong, and usefully so. No field was missing: `key_only`
- memberKey and nothing else - is sufficient for the client to apply a body
carrying a remote member row. What blocked every earlier attempt was that the
peer row reused a revision the client had already applied, and the client
applies one update per revision and drops every repeat (Lane M, opencode's
p2(39)). Shape variation was never being evaluated.

This also retires 20.49's reading: that run's apparent "key_only refused,
key_account acked" was the same artifact one level down - all its shapes shared
revision 5, so only the first was ever read.

### What is NOT settled, and why waiting cannot settle it

Whether the applied row makes the peer VISIBLE. Neither client has emitted a
membership dump since long before the peer bodies arrived:

  | | last membership dump | peer bodies received |
  |---|---|---|
  | Mac | t=91529 | t=220907, 225904, 230910 (size=3976) |
  | rig | t=54172 | - |

Every `peers valid: 0x1` reading on both machines predates the peer bodies by
minutes. `peer # 1` count of zero is ABSENCE OF MEASUREMENT, not measurement of
absence - the same trap as 20.49, caught the same way.

Nothing else on the client reports peer state: after t=230910 the only retail
sites still firing are 77/78/79 (`investment_bap_manager:drought`), 81, 85, 73.

Two readings remain, and the boot record cannot separate them:
  (a) the client dumps membership only during session-formation phases;
  (b) the client dumps on membership CHANGE, and applying our body changed
      nothing - it acked the revision and discarded the row.

Evidence against a simple orbit-trip probe: the Mac's transitions at t=116542
and t=122588 produced NO dumps, so a region change is not obviously a dump
trigger. Do not spend a boot on that assumption without a better reason.

### Next

The cheapest discriminator is not a log at all: both players were in the Tower
during this window, so ASK WHETHER EITHER GUARDIAN WAS VISIBLE. A yes settles
everything; a no leaves (a) and (b) open but costs nothing to obtain.

Failing that, the honest path is a client-side instrument on the membership
table - our own DLL - which needs the table located first, and that is Ghidra

## 20.49 THE SWEEP'S FIRST RUN TESTED TWO OF SIX SHAPES - AND SETTLED THE ONE
## BRANCH THAT MATTERED MOST: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS CONTENT-GATED. SOLO IS ACKED
## ON FIRST TRANSMISSION; full_mirror SURVIVES NINE REPUBLISHES UNACKED.
## (2026-08-25 ~17:01)

### Verified by execution

Peer-bearing bodies ran t=450034 -> t=477222 on session ...108 (the rig; the
Mac's session ...105 logged peer=0 throughout its solo window).

  - `full_mirror`: NINE bodies across 27 s, `ack=0` on every one.
  - `solo`: ONE body at t=477222. No membership body ever again.

The session did NOT end there. Traffic continued to t=833319 - another ~6
minutes, both key fingerprints present (4EE55ACA.. and FDEEB5CE..), svc=8
polls and keepalives flowing. `publishesMembership` is
`hasMembership && (regionChanged || !acknowledged(sessionId))`, and no region
changed, so the only thing that stops the loop is the acknowledgement landing.

Corroborated by size: the rig's membership-carrying keepalive at t=477223 is
`bytes=4754`; afterwards keepalives drop to the small no-body form (`bytes=835`
at t=477915). Note `membership=%u` in that line reports `hasMembership`, NOT
whether a body shipped - checked at activity_keepalive_push.cpp:295 rather than
assumed, because reading it as "a body shipped" would have inverted this whole
entry.

### What this settles

**Acknowledgement is content-gated, and the ack path works mid-session.** This
was the pre-named third branch and the one that would have been most expensive
to be wrong about: it was inferred from earlier boots that the client acks our
solo body, and that inference had been promoted to fact without ever being
tested under the current build. It now holds by execution. 20.48's reading
stands - the peer ROW is refused; the acknowledgement is not broken.

### The instrument bug that cost the other four shapes

`sweep_variant` anchored its phase to the first membership body of the BOOT
(t~325466, the Mac signing in alone), not to the first peer-bearing one. By the
time the rig joined at t=450034 the clock had already advanced
(450034 - 325466) / 30000 = 4.15 steps, so the sweep OPENED on index 4,
`full_mirror`, stepped to `solo`, and terminated. `key_only`, `key_account`,
`key_account_join` and `key_account_join_opaque` never shipped.

The 27-second peer window was not the user quitting and not a short-lived peer
condition - it was the sweep landing on its own terminal control almost
immediately.

Fixed in p2(40) with three corrections: anchor to the first PEER-BEARING body;
advance on a body COUNT rather than a wall clock, so a shape is measured by how
many transmissions carried it; and keep a time floor as well, because bodies
arrive in bursts (three inside one second at t=450034/450099/450919) and a pure
count would skip shapes the client never saw settle.

### Still open

Which field, or whether any second row is structurally acceptable at all. The
next run opens on `key_only` and walks. Pre-named: a peer variant acking names
the field; reaching `solo` again means no peer-bearing shape is acceptable and
the Ghidra lane should target table-level validation rather than field
semantics; `full_mirror` appearing as the FIRST variant line means the
anchoring is still wrong and the run is void.

Both machines booted on p2(34) (DLL-only deploy, server untouched). Verified by execution:

1. **A cross-client result was served AGAIN this boot** (server t=5319374,
   session_search served_descriptor=1 advertisement=0x4 bytes=146) - and STILL no contact
   attempt. Combined with 20.42: twice now, a client holding another client's descriptor
   has done nothing through any Steam surface.
2. **Identical choreography on BOTH machines, solo or not**: friends-table polls
   (table=0 slots 3 -> 43 -> 5, recurring; slot 3 re-polls minutes later), then exactly TWO
   create_lobby calls each (type=3 max=32, invented ids prefix|2 then prefix|3 - matching
   the descriptor's lobby field). This is sign-in/session scaffolding, NOT join behaviour:
   the sequence does not differ between a solo client and one that was just handed a peer.

   lobby. Serialized networking stays sign-in-only (cert->0, relay count->0) for the third
   boot running.

### What this eliminates

Every Steam-facing surface this shim exposes is now camera'd: serialized networking (p2(33)),
lobby methods + every unimplemented matchmaking slot, friends slots (p2(34)). Holding a
passive search result triggers NOTHING on any of them. The client-side join decision either
requires a trigger we do not provide, or runs on internal state we have not fed.

### The inference that reframes the front (marked as inference)

Retail D2 clients do not self-start joins from search results: the SERVER declares
membership ("you are in a fireteam/posse with X"), and the CLIENT then contacts X using
whatever identity/transport the platform offers. Our own logs show the receiving end of
that machine exists and is readable: `networking:session:membership:dump` with leader/
host peer indexes, peers-valid masks, and `[fireteam:*]` / `[posse:*]` structures - always
peer # 0 only. Upstream's in-process mod could poke that state directly; WE own the wire
equivalent already: the server pushes family rosters/membership tables today (the type-12
pushes carry member tables verbatim).

NEXT FRONT (proposed): make the standalone server declare BOTH players members of ONE
fireteam/posse in the pushed rosters - each client's own steamid string is already known -
and watch all three instrumented surfaces. If peer # 1 appears in the dumps, whichever door
the client knocks on hands us the transport contract. Pre-named negative: rosters updated +
dumps still 0x1 => the membership source the dump reads is client-authored, not
server-pushed => straight to the Ghidra lane on the client's join path.

Stride EXACTLY 6 bytes = 4-byte address + 2-byte port: an ARRAY OF BINARY ENDPOINT
STRUCTURES whose contents are the INJECTED PEER IDENTITY STRING, parsed as endpoints.

the client believes it must establish the peer connection, pulls a peer endpoint list,
and the list contains identity-string bytes where a real peer would carry real endpoint
bytes. The INTROs necessarily time out, the retry loop runs (stage 1), and setup:orbit
never completes. THE CLIENT-INTERNAL WAIT IS A NAT-TRAVERSAL RETRY LOOP AGAINST
GARBAGE ENDPOINTS.

CLAIM - WHERE THIS LEAVES THE ROAD. The forged record is adopted (roster names it) and
then feeds a CONNECTION-ESTABLISHMENT path that expects the peer's real transport
endpoint. The identity string reaches that path from somewhere we wrote or the game
copied: the slot's +0x50 identity-string field (a5's landing place, verified 20.162),
or a record field. For a REAL peer this either carries real endpoint bytes (written by
whomever fills +0x3c10/+0x3c20 - ADMIT's movups, never executed for us) or the DTLS
session description (20.144's plaintext establishment, absent this boot - the wire
carried no machine ids) replaces the dial entirely. The fix is therefore NOT more
record forging: it is naming who builds the endpoint array and what a real entry's
bytes are.

### RESULT 1 - `foreign=` IS A DEAD FLAG. RETRACT 20.170's READING OF IT.
20.170 RESULT 4 presented `foreign=0` as evidence that "the activity roster never lists

AND IT IS NEVER ASSIGNED. `grep -rn "activityJoinedForeignSession *=" Sunrise/src/`
returns NOTHING. Seven references in the whole tree: one declaration, six READS
(roster_snapshot:202, roster_report:43, keepalive_push:87/97/243/281), ZERO writes.

    peers. Do not use it as a peer diagnostic. 20.170's OTHER evidence for the same
    conclusion - neither client runs `Adding player` for the other's xuid - is

    the dead branch is not mistaken for live behaviour by the next reader.

`(mask_mask, count_mask, packed_mask, count_count, packed_packed, solo)`, but the actual
`TrailingVariant` enum (membership_sweep.h:44) is
`packedMasks, countMasks, packedMasksSeq, countMasksSeq, allMask, solo`. The deployed
`membership_sweep_pin = 0` therefore selects `packedMasks`, which MATCHES the log

### RESULT 2 - THE REAL GATE (VERIFIED-BY-READING + VERIFIED-BY-LOG)
The server FINDS the peer and PUBLISHES a peer row, then withdraws it permanently.
`ev=activity stage=membership_peer` fired 11 times in p2(110); the same shape three
times on three sessions:
```
  t=607478  included  key=0x846C8338F7D022E6 peer_row=1 first=0x00020002 second=0x3
  t=607518  included  key=0x846C8338F7D022E6 peer_row=1          <- 40 ms after the first
  t=607535  WITHDRAWN unacked=2 session=...107                    <- 17 ms later
  t=607589  membership_ack result=ok revision=1 session=...107    <- client answers, +54 ms

  ...105:  included 611588, included 616606, WITHDRAWN 621645, ack 621682  (+37 ms)
  ...108:  included 762541, included 762596, WITHDRAWN 766678, ack 766706  (+28 ms)
```
THE MECHANISM (activity_membership_push.cpp:277-320):
```c
  if (retry != nullptr && state::activity::membership::acknowledged(sessionId)) {
      retry->unackedPeerBodies = 0;          // budget resets only on an ack
  }
  bool publishPeer = havePeer && values.peerPresent
                     && (retry == nullptr || !retry->peerWithdrawn);
  if (publishPeer && ... retry->unackedPeerBodies >= settings.membershipPeerRetryCap) {
      retry->peerWithdrawn = true;           // ONE-WAY LATCH, per session
      publishPeer = false;
  }
  if (publishPeer) { apply_peer_row(...); ++retry->unackedPeerBodies; }
```
`peerWithdrawn` is a DELIBERATE one-way latch and the code says why:
  "The withdrawal flag is NOT cleared here: after a withdrawal the solo body gets
   acknowledged, and clearing on that would re-add the peer and restart the storm the
   cap exists to stop."
Once latched, `publishPeer` is false for the life of that session. The client therefore
never receives a peer row, never instantiates the peer player, and `Adding player` never
fires for the other xuid - which is exactly what 20.170 RESULT 4 measured on BOTH
machines. THE CHAIN FROM HERE TO "NO SECOND GUARDIAN" IS NOW CLOSED END TO END.

### RESULT 3 - THE DEFECT, NAMED: THE BUDGET IS COUNTED IN BODIES, SPENT IN MILLISECONDS
```
  source default   membershipPeerRetryCap{6}    (settings/server/definition.h:114)
  DEPLOYED VALUE   membership_peer_retry_cap = 2   (s1_accept/Sunrise/settings.json)
```
The peer appears during the LOAD BURST, when bodies go out ~40-55 ms apart
(607478->607518 = 40 ms; 762541->762596 = 55 ms). A cap of 2 therefore gives the client
a ~50 ms wall-clock deadline to acknowledge. That is shorter than the observed
client response time in every one of the three cases.
SCOPE / HONEST CAVEATS (L16, and they bound the fix):
  - The ack that lands after a withdrawal may be acking the peer-LESS body, since the
    withdrawal changes what is sent. "The client acked the peer body" is NOT established.
    What IS established: the client was responsive within 28-54 ms, and the budget was
    spent in ~50 ms of wall time.
  - Session ...105 is NOT the same case: included 611588 and 616606 are 5 s apart and the
    client sent NO ack for 15 s (last ack rev4 t=606594, next rev5 t=621682). Raising the
    cap plausibly fixes ...107 and ...108 and plausibly does NOT fix ...105. Do not
    pre-claim a full fix.
  - `havePeer` is true throughout: `foreign_member_identity` resolves, and the keepalive
    path still logs `membership_peer result=gained` AFTER each withdrawal (t=607602,
    t=763557). The server's STATE keeps the peer; only the PUBLISH is latched off.

### THE FIX SPACE, IN COST ORDER (none implemented - p2(111) tests only the first)
  (a) SETTINGS ONLY, no rebuild: raise `membership_peer_retry_cap` 2 -> 6 (the source
      default) and restart. This is BOOT_BRIEF_p2-111.md.
  (b) Make the budget TIME-based (or body-count AND elapsed-time) so a burst cannot spend
      it. Code change; the right fix if (a) shows the cap is directional but insufficient.
  (c) Clear `peerWithdrawn` on ack. The code comment explicitly warns this reopens the
      127-body storm that blocked a Tower load. Do NOT do this without a separate storm
      guard.
  (d) `activityJoinedForeignSession` never being set (RESULT 1) - a real defect, separate
      front, not on the milestone path.
DO NOT set the cap to 0: definition.h:111 records that disabling it is how the 127-body
storm became possible.

### RESULT 4 - THE BLOCK IS NOT RAW BYTES. THIS CORRECTS THE OBVIOUS GUESS.
Both region wrappers add a zero-initialised 4th argument and tail into the real readers
(A -> 0x1416D33C0, B -> 0x1416D3C30). Region A's reader:
```

  0x1416d33f9  jne  <skip>
  0x1416d33ff  call 0x140350ef0         ; READ ONE PRESENCE BIT
  0x1416d3406  je   <skip>              ; 0 -> this sub-chunk is ABSENT
  0x1416d340c  or   dword [rdi], 1      ; set bit 0 of the MASK
  0x1416d340f  lea  r9d, [rbp+0x40]     ; width = arg + 64
  0x1416d3428  lea  rdx, [rip+0x5c78e9] ; descriptor table
  0x1416d343a  call 0x14129aa80         ; the payload read
```
So REGION A IS A SERIES OF OPTIONAL SUB-CHUNKS, EACH PREFIXED BY A 1-BIT PRESENCE FLAG,
and the 9-bit "mask" the apply receives is BUILT BY THE READER from those wire bits - it
is not a field anyone sends. That is why `mask=0x1FF` (all nine present) is what the apply
passes on a full row, and it explains 20.145's "9-bit-masked copy of 8 verbatim
sub-chunks" from the other side of the wire.

WRONG, and shipping it would have produced a body the client mis-parses from the profile
bit onward, corrupting every later field including the trailing groups and the state hash.
Not shipping that guess was correct.

## *** SPECIFIED BIT BY BIT WITH NOTHING GUESSED, AND ITS ONE HAZARD (REGION A ***

Continuation of 20.176. Every width below was read from the decoder, not inferred.

### RESULT 1 - THE THREE REGION READERS, RESOLVED
```
  region A  entry+0x30   0x1416D3670 -> 0x1416D33C0   9 optional sub-chunks, returns bool
  region B  entry+0x118  0x1416D3DD0 -> 0x1416D3C30   ONE presence bit, then optional body
  tail      entry+0x1a0  0x14170F4F0                  FIXED, unconditional, no presence bit
```

### RESULT 2 - REGION A'S SUB-CHUNK TABLE (read from the code, in WIRE ORDER)
Each entry = one presence bit, then (if set) the payload. **THE WIRE ORDER IS NOT BIT
ORDER** - 0x100 is emitted FIFTH. An encoder driven off the mask value desyncs.
```
 # | mask  | payload read                                  | destination
 1 | 0x001 | 0x14129AA80: 16-bit words until a ZERO word,   | rsi+0x00 (128B)
   |       | max 64; then XOR-deobfuscated in the caller    |
 2 | 0x002 | 0x140A496E0                                    | rsi+0x80
 3 | 0x004 | read 8 bits                     -> word        | rsi+0xb0
 4 | 0x008 | read 6 bits (0x140351530), DEC  -> byte        | rsi+0xb2
 5 | 0x100 | read 6 bits (0x140351530), DEC  -> byte        | rsi+0xb3
 6 | 0x010 | 0x1416D3B20  (its result feeds `setne r15b`)   | rsi+0xb8
 7 | 0x020 | two 64-bit reads                               | -
 8 | 0x040 | 0x1404C74B0                                    | -
 9 | 0x080 | read 32 bits, then 0x1416BE1E0                 | rsi+0xe0
```
NOTE chunks 4 and 5 `dec al` AFTER the read: the stored byte is `read(6) - 1`. To store
0 you must write **1**. Writing 0 stores 0xFF.
Both bit readers are MSB-first over a 64-bit accumulator ([rcx+0x28] value, [rcx+0x30]
count, [rcx+0x24] position), so a 6-bit zero is six zero bits - the same convention our
`bits::Writer` already uses, which is why the client decodes our bodies today.

### RESULT 3 - THE TAIL (0x14170F4F0), FIXED AND UNCONDITIONAL
```
  read 32 -> [rdi+0x00]   read 32 -> [rdi+0x04]   read 32 -> [rdi+0x08]
  read  5 -> [rdi+0x0c]   read  2 -> [rdi+0x0d]   read flag -> [rdi+0x0e]
  then: test byte [rdi+0x0c], 0x10 ; je end   <- a CONDITIONAL extra section
```
104 bits minimum. **Bit 0x10 of the 5-bit field must be CLEAR** or a further section is
read and the stream desyncs.

### RESULT 4 - THE HAZARD, AND WHY THE MINIMAL WRITER IS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION
Region A returns bool. On FALSE the decoder SKIPS region B's read
(`0x14173c31e je 0x14173c33b`) while still reading the tail - so a false return desyncs
the body from that point on, corrupting the trailing groups and the state hash. Its exit:
```
  test r15b,r15b            -> false unless chunk 6 ran and failed
  call 0x1416BE1E0          -> name-terminator scan; TRUE iff a zero word exists in 64
  byte[rsi+0xb2] +1 <= 0x20 -> range check
  byte[rsi+0xb3] +1 <= 0x20 -> range check
  mov al,1
```
The minimal writer discharges ALL FOUR deterministically, without depending on the delta
buffer's prior contents (which nothing is proven to zero - the only two 0x7980 immediates
in .text are the comparator's memcmp and one in the diff, neither a memset):
  - chunk 6 ABSENT -> `setne r15b` never runs -> r15b keeps its entry value 1.
  - chunk 1 PRESENT with a single 0x0000 word -> word[0] deobfuscates to
    (0 * 0x7b4f) XOR 0 = 0 -> the scan finds its terminator at index 0 -> TRUE.
  - chunks 4 and 5 PRESENT with 6-bit value 1 -> stored 1-1 = 0 -> 0+1 = 1 <= 0x20, twice.

### RESULT 5 - THE WRITER CONTRACT (drop-in for `write_player_delta`)
Replace `writer.write(kPlayerProfileAbsent, kFlagWidth)` with, when enabled:
```
  write(1, 1)                    // profile-present            entry+0x21
  write(header1, 32)             //                            entry+0x24
  write(header2 + 1, 3)          // decoder DECs it            entry+0x28
  // --- region A, 9 presence bits IN WIRE ORDER ---
  write(1, 1); write(0, 16)      // #1 0x001 name: one zero word = terminator
  write(0, 1)                    // #2 0x002 absent
  write(0, 1)                    // #3 0x004 absent
  write(1, 1); write(1, 6)       // #4 0x008 -> byte 0xb2 = 0
  write(1, 1); write(1, 6)       // #5 0x100 -> byte 0xb3 = 0
  write(0, 1)                    // #6 0x010 absent  (KEEPS r15b = 1)
  write(0, 1)                    // #7 0x020 absent
  write(0, 1)                    // #8 0x040 absent
  write(0, 1)                    // #9 0x080 absent
  // --- region B ---
  write(0, 1)                    // absent
  // --- tail, fixed ---
  write(t0,32); write(t1,32); write(t2,32);
  write(t3, 5);                  // bit 0x10 MUST be clear
  write(t4, 2); write(t5, 1);
```
Total 150 bits. Suggested initial values, REPLAYED from the p2(113) harvest rather than
invented (region A's tail bytes were 00*11, 01, 01, then zeros):
`header1=0, header2=0, t0=0, t1=0, t2=0x01000000, t3=1, t4=0, t5=0`.

### WHAT THIS WRITER DOES AND DOES NOT DO
It sets `pc=1` on the peer's player row with an EMPTY profile. It will NOT render a
guardian - there is no name, no appearance, and region A carries identity only (20.173
R3). It is the decoder-correct minimum that tests whether the present bit alone changes
client behaviour, and it is the scaffold every richer block is written into.
A FULL block additionally needs the payload encodings of chunks 2, 6, 7, 8, 9
(0x140A496E0, 0x1416D3B20, 0x1404C74B0, 0x1416BE1E0's writer side) - all unread.
NO HASH IS REQUIRED anywhere: the wire apply passes verify=0 (20.174 R2, corroborated at
runtime 20.175 R3).

## 20.188 *** p2(116): THE DECODER REJECTS OUR PROFILE BLOCK. ret=0 ON THE ***
## *** PLAYER-BEARING BODY, ret=1 ON THE MEMBERS-ONLY BODY. OUR BYTES *WERE* THE ***
## *** PROBLEM, AND THE STAGING/STAGE-GATE LANES ARE BOTH DOWNSTREAM OF A BODY THE ***
## *** CLIENT NEVER ACCEPTS. ROW BASE = 0x4240, SETTLED. (2026-08-30, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE DECODE VERDICT (the pre-named CONTENT NEGATIVE of BOOT_BRIEF_p2-116)
    call=1  members=2 players=0  ret=0x1 ok=1  -> apply fires
    call=2  members=2 players=1  ret=0x0 ok=0  -> NO APPLY
The decoder 0x14173BFC0 returns FALSE for the body carrying our player row and its
profile block, and TRUE for the members-only body. Its caller 0x1416E33AC tests AL and
branches to the `[rbx+9]=1` abort store on zero (VERIFIED-BY-READING), so the apply is
never scheduled for that body - which is why no apply ever ran on a live player row.
n=1 for the failing case (the run captured one cycle) but it is the exact negative the
brief pre-named, and the paired positive in the same millisecond controls for it.

### RESULT 2 - THE HEADLINE IS OVERTURNED
"OUR BYTES WERE NEVER THE PROBLEM" (STATE, 20.183-20.185) is FALSE. Delivery and ack
(20.182 R1) were real but proved only that the body arrived; nothing had ever logged the
decoder's verdict. The whole wedge narrative rested on applies that carried players=1 -
and the struct at 0x3BE1300 is REUSED, so a FAILED decode leaves players=1 and a partial
row in it for the NEXT members-only apply to read as stale debris. That single mechanism
explains 20.187's run-to-run variance, 20.183's "row present but never applied", and
20.184's "identity fields zero with foreign data nearby" - all one artifact.
CONSEQUENCE: the staging-object lane (20.183-20.185) and the stage-6..9 gate map are both
DOWNSTREAM of a body the client rejects at decode. Neither is refuted; both are unreachable
until the block decodes. Do not spend another boot on either first.

### RESULT 3 - ROW BASE SETTLED: 0x4240 (closes 20.184 R1)
    base=0x4240  populated: +0x14 01 | +0x18 01 07 8e c2 f1 a2 44 a6 fd | +0x24 01 | +0x31 01
    base=0x4280  64 bytes, ALL ZERO
    base=0x43c0  zero except 0808 near the end
0x4280 is the inter-row gap, not the row. The decoder wrote the row's identity fields and
then failed, so the failure is IN THE PROFILE BLOCK, after the gate bit.

### RESULT 4 - THE PRIME SUSPECT: OUR REGION-B ENCODING (one bit vs four)
`write_minimal_profile` emits region B as a SINGLE presence bit set to zero
(session_messages.cpp:278, "Region B: one presence bit, body absent"). The region-B lane
reported the same night that the region-B WIRE shape is "4 presence bits + optional
obfuscated name + 3 tiny DEC'd fields". If that is right, we underrun the bitstream at
region B and every field after it - the whole 104-bit tail - is read at the wrong offset,
which is exactly the shape of a decoder that parses the identity fine and then returns
false. UNVERIFIED: the two readings come from different lanes and have not been
reconciled against the decoder's own region-B reader. That reconciliation is the next
job and it is static - no boot.

### RESULT 5 - WHAT THIS BOOT COST AND WHAT IT BOUGHT
One solo mac run, ~3 min, read-only, staging detour disarmed and confirmed disarmed
(`staging_populate=0` in the install line, zero `stage=staging` lines). It converted the
project's central open question from "why is our correct block ignored" to "our block is
rejected, here is where to look" - and settled a row base that two prior sessions left
open. The instrument that did it was one captured return value.

## 20.190 *** p2(118) IS A FALSE NEGATIVE: THE DETOUR FIRED 8/8 EXACTLY AS DESIGNED, ***
## *** BUT profile_ingress HAD ALREADY SPENT ITS ENTIRE 8-LINE BUDGET ON LOCAL COMMITS ***
## *** 35 SECONDS EARLIER. THE OBSERVER WAS BLIND WHEN THE EXPERIMENT RAN. ***
## *** (2026-08-30, L13 AS CODE) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE WRITE DETOUR WORKED MECHANICALLY (VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION)
8 substitutions, `nth=1..8`, every one on a player-bearing body with `discarded_r8=0x0`:
    ev=dtrace stage=staging call=2 nth=1 players=1 discarded_r8=0x0
      staging=0x6FFFFC2BB7A0 regionA=0x6FFFFC2BB690 tail=0x6FFFFC2BB780 mask=0x109
Zero `why=non_null_r8` skips, so the p2(117) measurement reproduced exactly: every
player-bearing apply arrives with NULL. No crash, no hang, the client ran the full dwell.
This project's first write detour shipped and behaved precisely as specified.

### RESULT 2 - AND THE BOOT STILL COULD NOT ANSWER ITS OWN QUESTION
`profile_ingress` gates its ENTIRE report - the `ev=ingress stage=apply` summary line
included - behind one shared `kDumpCap = 8`. The local registry commits fire in a burst
during load and spent all eight slots at t=58188..71062. The staging window opened at
t=106490. A wire-path fire in that window would have produced NO OUTPUT AT ALL.
So "zero wire fires" in p2(118) measures the observer, not the client. Same defect
retroactively voids the same claim in 20.189 R3 (withdrawn in place).

### RESULT 3 - THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, NAMED PRECISELY
One budget shared by two caller classes with wildly different timing: the local path is a
load-time burst, the wire path is a steady trickle that starts a minute later. The burst
always wins. This is L13 exactly - a null result indicts the instrument first - and it is
the SECOND time this session that a cap or a rotation destroyed the evidence for the
question under test (20.187 R5 was the first, a client log overwritten).
FIX SHIPPED: separate budgets per caller class, classified by whether the return address
lands inside the apply's .pdata bounds (0x1781800..0x17834CE = WIRE, else local). The wire
path now has 8 dumps the local path cannot touch, the one-line summary is capped at 96
rather than 8, and every line carries `path=WIRE` or `path=local` so the class is readable
without decoding an RVA by eye.

### RESULT 4 - THE STANDING RULE THIS EARNS
A capped observer must not share its budget across event classes whose rates differ. Cap
per class, and cap the cheap summary line far higher than the expensive hex dumps. Any
observer whose cap can be exhausted by a DIFFERENT event than the one under test is not an
instrument, it is a coin flip.

## *** WHAT WAS SUPPRESSING IT. NULL IS THE NORMAL, WORKING STATE FOR THIS PATH; THE ***
## *** REGION-B DECODE FIX WAS THE WHOLE UNLOCK. (2026-08-30, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION) ***

### RESULT 1 - FIRST WIRE-PATH PROFILE APPLY IN THE PROJECT'S HISTORY
    t=110159 ev=ingress stage=apply call=14 path=WIRE caller_rva=0x178245D index=0

`caller_rva=0x178245D` is the return address of the helper call at 0x141782458 - the WIRE

### RESULT 2 - THE SUBSTITUTION SUPPRESSED IT (the inversion)
Apply calls, third argument, and whether we substituted:
    apply#2..#9   t=103200..109090  arg3=NULL  stage=4  SUBSTITUTED (cap 8)  -> 0 wire fires
    apply#10      t=110158          arg3=NULL  stage=4  NOT substituted      -> WIRE FIRE
The cap ran out, the client got its own NULL back, and the helper fired within 1 ms. During

The staging-population lane is DEAD as a fix. Its premise - "the apply cannot work because

What actually unlocked the wire path was the p2(117) region-B fix - one bit to four. The
"no wire fires" readings that made the staging lane look necessary were the profile_ingress
cap (20.190), not the client.

### RESULT 4 - THE CONFOUND, STATED HONESTLY, AND HOW IT CLOSES
The substitution cap expiring and the first wire fire coincide within one apply call, so a
weaker reading survives: the helper needs N stage-4 applies before it fires, and the cap
merely happened to expire first. The discriminator costs nothing - DISARM the detour
(settings flip, no rebuild) and re-run. If wire fires appear from apply#2 onward, RESULT 2
is confirmed and the detour is retired. If they still only appear around apply#10, the
substitution was innocent and something else gates on call count.
`client.staging_populate` set to FALSE for that run.

The helper's argument register r9 reads mask=0x1FF and a8 reads hash=0xFFFFFFFF, neither of
which is what our block carries (mask 0x109, hdr1 0). Either those registers are not the
mask/hash on the wire call site (the observer's mapping was derived from the LOCAL caller),
or the apply rebuilds them. Not chased; recorded.

reading and never tested against the null hypothesis that NULL IS THE NORMAL STATE. U2 says
instrument before intervention; the instrument that settled this (a return value and a
caller-class label) cost nothing and existed all along.

## 20.195 *** p2(123): A REAL NAME CROSSES THE WIRE, BYTE-EXACT, BOTH DIRECTIONS. THE ***

## 20.196 *** OPTION B ANSWERED WITHOUT A BOOT: APPEARANCE DOES NOT CROSS THE ***
## *** CLIENT<->CLIENT CHANNEL. IT IS 98.7% 42-BYTE HEARTBEATS WITH NO BURST AT ***
## *** CO-LOCATION AND A 234-BYTE LIFETIME MAXIMUM. THE SERVER LANE IS THE RIGHT ***
## *** LANE. (2026-08-30, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION, p2(110) pcap) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE PEER CHANNEL CARRIES A HEARTBEAT AND NOTHING ELSE
p2(110)'s paired capture, flow 192.168.1.164:3097 <-> 192.168.1.136:3097 (the direct
client<->client channel; classified BY FLOW PAIR per 20.167, not by a fixed port):
    2774 packets / 117,225 bytes over 342 s
    size histogram: 2756 x 42 B, then 8 x 37, 2 x 58, 2 x 138, 2 x 124, 1 each of 26/60/217/234
    42-byte packets carry 115,752 B = 98.7% of the channel's entire lifetime traffic
    LARGEST PACKET EVER SENT: 234 bytes
A guardian's appearance - gear hashes across every slot, shaders, ornaments, the folded
material pairs of character_appearance_render - cannot be expressed in 42-byte heartbeats
whose largest outlier in a whole session is 234 bytes.

### RESULT 2 - AND THERE IS NO BURST WHEN THE PEER ARRIVES
Bytes per 10 s bucket from the channel's FIRST packet (i.e. from co-location):
    t+0s 4391 B / t+10s 3444 / t+20s 3402 / t+30s 3444 / t+40s 3402 / t+50s 3444 ...
Flat from the first bucket onward. If appearance crossed this channel it would arrive as a
one-time transfer at co-location and that bucket would tower over the rest. It does not
exist. The channel is shaped for liveness, not for bulk.

### RESULT 3 - THE CONTRAST THAT MAKES THE POINT
The client<->SERVER gameplay channel (UDP 30976) in the same capture carries the same
42-byte heartbeat PLUS real payload variety - 214 x 58 B, and 538-byte packets at the top.
So bulk DOES ride the server channel and does NOT ride the peer channel. The two channels
are not the same shape and the difference is visible in one histogram.

### RESULT 4 - THE DECISION THIS UNBLOCKS
Option B is answered: a peer's appearance does NOT arrive over the client<->client channel,
so building root->account resolution on the server is NOT wasted work. The character_record
lane (20.173's gap: the snapshot path selects its account from the CONNECTION and no
root->account resolution exists tree-wide) is the correct next front.
COST: zero boots. The answer was in a capture this project took on 2026-08-29 and had never
histogrammed - U1 COROLLARY again (the oracle you already hold is the one you forget to
open), the third time this session.

### RESULT 5 - THE CAVEAT, AND WHY IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE DECISION
p2(110) predates the working profile path, so strictly this proves the channel carried no
appearance THEN. A defender of the peer-channel theory would say transfer only begins once
profile rows apply. Against that: p2(110) was a healthy co-located paired session with both
players present and transport symmetric, and the channel shows no bulk CAPACITY at all - no
fragmentation, no size variety, nothing above 234 B in 2774 packets. A channel that has
never carried more than 234 bytes is not the one delivering a character. Confirming with a
capture during a CURRENT paired run costs one boot and can ride along with any future paired
test; it does not need its own.

### RESULT 6 - AN ENVIRONMENT TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE IT COST ANYTHING
ENVIRONMENTS recorded (20.166, measured 2026-08-29) that the route to the rig is en0. It is
now en13: the user is on ethernet rather than Wi-Fi. The interface is NOT a constant - it
follows whichever link is active, and `arp -n 192.168.1.136` lists the rig on BOTH en0 and
en13, so ARP cannot disambiguate it. A capture on the documented-but-stale en0 would have
produced an empty pcap and read as a clean null. ALWAYS resolve
`route -n get 192.168.1.136` at capture time, and when in doubt capture BOTH interfaces:
the server binds 192.168.1.164 (en0) while client->rig traffic egresses via the route, so a
paired session can be genuinely split across two interfaces.

## 20.197 *** p2(124): IDENTITY LANDS, BUT BYTE-REVERSED - WE USED A RAW-BYTE WRITER FOR A ***
## *** VALUE FIELD. THE SUBSCRIPTION QUESTION IS UNANSWERED, NOT ANSWERED: THE CLIENT WAS ***
## *** HANDED A MALFORMED SOID. (2026-08-30, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE VALUES ARE RIGHT, THE BYTE ORDER IS WRONG
Predicted stored bytes at regionA +0xc0: `000110000130AA9E 010110000130AA9E`.
Observed on the WIRE path, both machines: `9EAA300100100100 9EAA300100100101`.
That is the same pair BYTE-REVERSED. The client's OWN local commit stores the little-endian
form (`000110000130AA9E...`, mac call=1), so the wire path and the local path disagree and
ours is the one that is wrong.
CAUSE: `bits::write_raw_u64` writes LOW BYTE FIRST, and chunk 7's reader is
`read_wide(0x40)` - a 64-bit VALUE read, most-significant-bit first, whose result is stored
as a host integer. bit_raw.h states the distinction in its own header comment: "Raw fields
copy bytes and keep engine order. VALUE fields are most-significant-bit first." We reached
for the helper that the neighbouring playerId field uses without checking that playerId's
READER is a byte-wise raw read while chunk 7's is not. Two conventions coexist inside one
body and THE FIELD decides which applies, not the C++ type.
FIX: `writer.write(soid, 64)`. Shipped.

### RESULT 2 - THE IDENTITY SELECTION LOGIC IS CORRECT, AND THE RIG PROVED IT
slot 1 published account `9EAA300100110100` and character `9EAA300100110103` (byte-reversed
on the wire, but those are the values). The RIG's OWN local harvest independently reads
`000111000130AA9E 030111000130AA9E` = the same account and the same character `...0103`.
So the selected-character walk picked exactly what the rig itself considers selected. The
boot brief's caveat ("the character half assumes index 1") was right to be a caveat - the
selected character is index 3 - and the ACCOUNT half matched with no caveat at all.

### RESULT 3 - THE CLAIM IS UNANSWERED (and the brief pre-named this exact case)
    14 `ev=queuez stage=subscribe_in`, 0 FOREIGN roots (baseline p2(123): 13, 0)
Every root is still the requester's own. But this does NOT answer the question, because the
identity the client received was malformed: a byte-reversed SOID has a completely different
high band (`0x000110000130AA9E` vs the `0x9EAA3001...` account band), so a client doing any
band validation at all would discard it before forming a request. BOOT_BRIEF_p2-124 named
this precisely - "SECOND CONTENT NEGATIVE: the identity bytes do NOT match the prediction...
the subscription question is unanswered this boot - the client was told nothing coherent."
Do not record p2(124) as evidence that clients ignore peer identity. It is evidence that
they ignore GARBAGE peer identity, which is unsurprising and uninformative.

### RESULT 4 - EVERYTHING ELSE HELD
Decode 40/40 ok=1 on both machines with the larger body (chunk 7 adds 128 bits per row,
mask 0x109 -> 0x129). Liveness clean, `staging_populate=0` both machines. The name from
20.195 continues to arrive. The third negative in the brief (a size limit at the larger
body) did not occur.

### RESULT 5 - THE BLACK SCREEN, FOURTH DATA POINT
    p2-121  313.3 s idle -> BLACK      p2-122    0.0 s idle -> no black
    p2-123   89.6 s idle -> BLACK      p2-124  102.3 s idle -> BLACK
Still monotone, still only ONE negative case, and the negative is the only run where the mac
did not sit alone. n=4. It survived a name being added (p2-123) and identity being added
(p2-124), so content is not the variable. Recorded, not chased.

## 20.198 *** p2(125): THE IDENTITY ARRIVES PERFECTLY AND THE CLIENT STILL NEVER ASKS FOR ***
## *** THE PEER'S RECORD. THERE IS NO PULL. AND THE EXISTING PUSH IS SELF-ONLY BY ***
## *** CONSTRUCTION. THE APPEARANCE FRONT IS NOT A BROKEN LOOKUP - IT IS A MISSING ***
## *** DELIVERY MECHANISM. (2026-08-30, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE BYTE-ORDER FIX LANDED, PREDICTION EXACT
regionA off=192, WIRE path, both machines - and each holds the PEER's identity:
    mac call=128  000111000130AA9E 030111000130AA9E   <- the RIG's account + character
    rig call=12   000110000130AA9E 010110000130AA9E   <- the MAC's account + character
    (call=1 on each machine is its own local commit, for contrast)
Byte-for-byte the p2(125) prediction. `writer.write(soid, 64)` is the correct encoder for
chunk 7; `bits::write_raw_u64` was not (20.197 R1). Decode 40/40 ok=1 on both machines.
So each client now knows, in well-formed shape and in the right SOID band, exactly which
account and which character its peer is.

### RESULT 2 - AND IT CHANGES NOTHING: 14 subscribe_in, 0 FOREIGN
    p2(123) name only                 13 subscribe_in / 0 foreign
    p2(124) identity, byte-reversed   14 / 0   (uninformative - malformed, 20.197 R3)
    p2(125) identity, WELL-FORMED     14 / 0   <- THE REAL NEGATIVE
Every root is still the requester's own. This is the CONTENT NEGATIVE
BOOT_BRIEF_p2-124/125 pre-named, and now it is clean: the client has the peer's identity,
correctly encoded, and does not request that peer's record. THE CLIENT DOES NOT PULL PEER
CHARACTER RECORDS. Telling it who the peer is does not make it ask.

### RESULT 3 - THE PUSH PATH IS SELF-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY OVERSIGHT
`queuez_banner_push.cpp` reaches `snapshot::prepare_roster_appearance_refresh` through
    const state::AccountState account = state::account_snapshot(after.accountKey);
i.e. the account of the CONNECTION being served, then matches a characterSoid within THAT
account before preparing anything. So the one appearance-bearing path this server has pushes
each client its OWN roster and cannot express another account's. That is 20.173's
observation, now confirmed as the operative constraint rather than a missing lookup.

### RESULT 4 - WHAT THIS DOES TO THE CHARACTER_RECORD LANE (the decision this boot bought)
The lane as scoped - "add root->account resolution so a foreign root resolves" - is DEAD:
there is no foreign root to resolve, because nothing asks. A resolution added today would
sit in a code path that never runs.
What remains is materially larger and materially more speculative: AUTHOR a delivery of a
peer's character record - a push the client never requests - and hope the client has a
consumer for it. Nothing yet establishes that such a consumer exists. Before any of that is
built, the question to answer is: does the client have ANY route that accepts another
account's character record? That is static/RE work on the client, not server engineering,
and it is where the appearance front now sits.
COST OF LEARNING THIS: two boots (p2(124)+p2(125)), one of which was spent on my own
byte-order bug. Cheap against writing a resolution layer that would never have executed.

### RESULT 5 - WHAT IS SOLID AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-LITIGATED
The membership profile pipeline is DONE and proven to carry arbitrary authored content in
both directions: shape (20.194), a name (20.195), and now real per-player identity in the
client's own SOID band (this entry). Nothing about the appearance wall is a defect in that
pipeline.

### RESULT 6 - BLACK SCREEN, FIFTH POINT
    p2-121 313.3s BLACK | p2-122 0.0s no black | p2-123 89.6s BLACK
    p2-124 102.3s BLACK | p2-125 (this run) BLACK
Five runs, one negative, and the negative remains the only run where the mac did not sit
alone before the peer arrived. It has now survived an empty block, a name, a malformed
identity and a well-formed identity - content is definitively not the variable.

## *** PER-PLAYER POINTER - IDENTICAL FOR BOTH ROWS. THE HELPER INDEXES PLAYERS ***

    mac  index=0 dest=0x4631FA8      rig  index=0 dest=0x28003151FA8
    mac  index=1 dest=0x4631FA8      rig  index=1 dest=0x28003151FA8
One distinct value per machine, and it is the SAME pointer the dtrace apply hook logs as

## 20.200 *** p2(127): THE PUBLISHED NAME IS FOUND IN CLIENT MEMORY AT session+0x3b80 - ***
## *** BUT ON ONLY 1 SCAN IN 24. THE WIRE PROFILE REACHES MEMORY AND DOES NOT PERSIST ***
## *** THERE. AND THE BLACK-SCREEN IDLE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED. (2026-08-30) ***

### RESULT 1 - THE LANDMARK IS REAL, AND ITS OFFSET IS MEASURED NOT DERIVED
    rig call=23 path=WIRE index=1 base=0x190D3D01FA8 hits=0x3b80
The UTF-16LE bytes of a name THIS SERVER PUBLISHED were found in the client's session object
at +0x3b80. That is the first time this project has located its own authored content in
client memory by search rather than by offset arithmetic, and it sits near - but equal to
none of - the three contradictory disassembly candidates (0x3b58 / 0x3c00 / 0x3c68).

### RESULT 2 - AND IT IS NOT RESIDENT: 1 HIT IN 24 SCANS
23 of 24 scans returned `hits=none`, across both machines, both paths, both row indices,
over the whole dwell. A per-player profile store would hold the name continuously once
written; this does not. Readings, in order of what the evidence supports:
 (a) INSTRUMENT FLAW, and it is the most likely: the scan runs at helper ENTRY, BEFORE the
     original writes. It can only ever see what a PREVIOUS call left behind. Scanning after
     the pass-through call is the obvious correction and it costs nothing.
 (b) the 0x3b80 location is transient scratch the helper writes through, not the persistent
     per-player entry, and the real store is outside the 0x10000 window.
 (c) the client accepts the profile and does not retain it - which would explain the whole
     appearance wall, and is exactly the kind of conclusion NOT to reach off one hit.
DO NOT record (c) as a finding. The next boot discriminates (a) from (b)/(c) for free by
moving the scan after the original call and widening the window.

### RESULT 3 - THE BLACK-SCREEN IDLE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED (my overstatement, corrected)
    p2-121 313.3s BLACK | p2-122   0.0s clean | p2-123  89.6s BLACK
    p2-124 102.3s BLACK | p2-125  93.8s BLACK | p2-126   0.0s clean
    p2-127  87.1s CLEAN  <-- breaks it
p2(127) idled 87.1 s - squarely inside the range that blacked four times - and BOTH machines
rendered fine throughout. Idle time does not predict the black screen. I called this
"essentially settled" after n=6 with two negatives at the extreme; that was overstated from
a correlation with no mechanism behind it, and the seventh point refutes it. The honest
status returns to: intermittent, unexplained, no error line ever accompanies it, and NOT
correlated with anything we publish (it survived an empty block, a name, and identity, and
now it has failed to appear at an idle that previously always produced it).
What DID change for p2(126)/p2(127) is the client DLL (entry dump, then the landmark scan) -
observation-only changes that should not affect rendering, which makes coincidence the
leading explanation and is itself a reason to stop reading tea leaves from n=7.

## 20.201 *** p2(128): THE PEER'S PROFILE PERSISTS, THE ARRAY IS MEASURED (base 0x3b80, ***
## *** stride 0x1a8), AND IT IS THE SAME ARRAY THE GATHER FUNCTION WALKS. REGION A ***
## *** CHUNK 2 IS THE 48 BYTES THAT FUNCTION READS AS THREE SIMD VECTORS. ***

### RESULT 3 - IT IS THE SAME ARRAY THE GATHER FUNCTION WALKS (the link this lane wanted)
The gather at 0x140D48490 reads `[rcx + rdi + 0x3c00/0x3c10/0x3c20]` with
`imul rcx, rax, 0x1a8`. Against the MEASURED base:
    0x3c00 - 0x3b80 = 0x80
    -> the three 16-byte vectors are entry+0x80, +0x90, +0xa0 (48 bytes, 0x80..0xaf)
And 20.179 R2 places region A chunk #2 at rsi+0x80: a 288-bit read copied 36 B VERBATIM
into a 40-byte zeroed slot.
=> CHUNK 2 OCCUPIES THE FIRST 40 OF THE 48 BYTES THE GATHER FUNCTION READS AS THREE SIMD
VECTORS AND EMITS INTO A 48-BYTE-STRIDE OUTPUT LIST.
Corroboration: the byte that gather compares, session+0x3c68, is entry+0xe8 - exactly one
byte past region A's 232-byte (0xe8) span. The whole layout is now self-consistent.

### RESULT 3b - CORRECTION, SAME NIGHT: THE "THREE VECTORS" ARE A 48-BYTE STRUCT COPY
Asked whether the rest was derivable statically, it was - from data already on disk, and it
overturns my own reading above. The profile_harvest dump gives each client's OWN chunk 2
(regionA off=128 = entry+0x80):
    mac  C59EAA3001001001 0000...  (40 further bytes ALL ZERO)
    rig  C69EAA3001001001 0000...  (40 further bytes ALL ZERO)
Read as floats that is garbage (1.24e-09, 2.64e-38, 0, 0); read as a big-endian qword it is
0xC59EAA3001001001 / 0xC69EAA3001001001 - a SOID-family IDENTIFIER in a 0xC5/0xC6 band,
followed by 40 zero bytes.
So the gather's `movups` triple is NOT three semantic vectors. It is a compiler-vectorised
48-BYTE STRUCT COPY of a region that holds one 8-byte id and padding. "Transform-shaped"
was me reading an SSE memcpy idiom as geometry, which is exactly the over-interpretation
this project keeps paying for. RESULT 4's caution about visual corruption is moot; there is
no geometry here to corrupt.
WHAT THE GATHER ACTUALLY DOES: walks players, copies each one's 48-byte chunk-2 region into
a counted output list. That is an ID GATHER - plausibly "the set of character ids present" -
not a draw list.
AND THE SHARP CONSEQUENCE: our writer emits chunk 2 ABSENT, and its 40-byte destination is
only zeroed by the chunk-2 reader, which does not run when the chunk is absent. So a PEER's
entry+0x80 holds zero where the local player's holds a real identifier - and the gather
emits a zero id for the peer. THAT is the next experiment, and it is far more specific than
"write chunk 2 with known values": write the peer's real 0xC5-band id.
OPEN, and it must be measured not guessed: that id is NOT a plain function of the account
SOID. Both machines' own chunk 2 read ...3001001001 despite the rig's account being
0x9EAA300100110100, so the middle field does not track the account. Where the client gets
0xC59EAA3001001001 is unresolved and is the first thing to establish before writing it.

### RESULT 4 - WHAT THIS MEANS, STATED WITHOUT STRETCHING IT
This is the first direct link from a field WE CAN WRITE to a function that assembles
per-player data into what looks like a draw or instance list. It is NOT proof that chunk 2
is appearance, and three 16-byte vectors read as a unit is transform-shaped (position /
rotation / scale, or a 3x4 matrix) rather than gear-shaped.
Our writer currently emits chunk 2 ABSENT, so those 48 bytes hold whatever the client put
there. The experiment that follows is therefore small and completely defined: write chunk 2
with known values and observe what the gather emits - and whether anything moves, deforms or
disappears on screen. That is a one-setting server change on a pipeline already proven to
carry verbatim content byte-exact.
CAUTION FOR THAT EXPERIMENT: this writes into data a render path consumes on a machine we
do not control the failure modes of. Author it behind its own default-false setting, put
sane values in (the client's own bytes, read back from a dump, are the safest first
content), and expect visual corruption as a SUCCESS signal, not a crash.

### RESULT 2 - MY PROCESS FAILURES, NAMED
(a) I derived a 396-byte layout from SUMMARY docs and shipped it without reading the
    instruction trail, against STATE's "PREFER LANDMARKS OVER ARITHMETIC" - the rule that
    exists because offset derivation has been wrong here three times.
(b) I budgeted the variant table at "first 2 snapshots" rather than "first 2 PLAYER-BEARING

    capture's two gaps were real, but the derivation has now cost a boot.

### RESULT 3 - THE STRUCTURAL ERROR (this is the one that matters)
l9-profile-layout CLAIM 3 says the session layer copies the profile VERBATIM, and I read
that as "the stored bytes are a pure function of what our encoder writes". It is not.
VERBATIM covers the DELTA->STATE hop only. The WIRE->DELTA hop is the bit reader, and it
TRANSFORMS: chunks 4/5 and header 2 are read then DECREMENTED (already known), and the
name is run through the cipher. Any field whose reader applies a transform we have not
read is a field whose stored value we cannot predict. I modelled wire values as stored
values wherever I had no better information.

### RESULT 4 - PROVEN ON HELD DATA: THE STORED NAME IS A THIRD FORM
RE_output/captures/p2-113_profile_harvest/call1_regionA.bin (a REAL client region A we
have held since 2026-08-29) decodes to "Player" ONLY under
    plain[i] = ((stored[i] ^ key16(i)) * 0xBBAF) & 0xFFFF
which is name_codec's ENCODE applied to the stored words, i.e. stored = decode(plain).
Neither of p2(133)'s two enumerated name forms (raw plain, or the wire form
((plain^key)*INV)) is that. `name_codec.py --try-both` exists for exactly this question
and I did not run it until after the boot.

### RESULT 5 - CORRECTIONS TO THE RAW TRAIL, READ FROM INSTRUCTIONS
- The masked copy 0x1416d2fc0 gates [0xb3..0xb4) on BIT 8 (`shr eax,8`), not on bit 0
  "re-tested" as the raw notes record.
- The apply passes mask 0x1ff UNCONDITIONALLY (`mov [rsp+0x20],0x1ff` @0x141782450), so
  every chunk is copied from the delta regardless of what the wire declared present.
- Helper A's `je 0x1417afa54` does NOT skip the masked copy: 0x1417afa54 is
  `mov r14b,1; jmp 0x1417af96d`, which re-enters it. Region A IS written on apply.
- The apply's delta offsets are region A@+0x28, region B@+0x110, tail@+0x198 - eight
  BELOW CLAIM 5's table, which is consistently +8 throughout.
- The +8 table-base question is resolved: helper B writes entry+0x108 at state+0x3c68,
  and the hashed buffer starts 8 bytes above the apply's base, so 0x3c68-8 = 0x3c60 =
  15192+264 = the fork's HISTORICAL base. Arm A's 9/9 acceptance and this arithmetic
  agree; `session_state_client_base` FALSE is correct and the p2(129) shift is dead.
- The harvested tail (call1_tail.bin) is 20 ZERO bytes, while our encoder publishes
  kProfileTailWord2 = 0x01000000. Another wire-vs-stored value to establish, not assume.

### RESULT 6 - WHERE THIS LEAVES THE FRONT
The causal finding (20.205) is untouched: the profile block breaks the state hash, proven
both directions. What is dead is the DERIVED image. Predicting the stored bytes requires
the bit reader's per-field wire->delta semantics (0x14173BFC0), which no lane has walked -
or a direct read of the client's stored player entry. The system is parked in the arm A
configuration (publish_player_profile FALSE), which is measured stable.

## 20.212 *** THE SLOT ARITHMETIC CONFLICT: OUR JOIN GRANT HANDS OUT 7,936 OF 8,192
## *** SLOTS, LEAVING 256 GRANTABLE - THE CLIENT WANTS >=4,096. THE TYPE-20/0

### RESULT 1 - THE FORK'S SLOT MACHINERY IS COMPLETE AND WAS NEVER EXERCISED
entity_slot_request::kMessageType = 20 (activity_entity_slot_request_parser.h). The route
handles type 20 -> prepare_grant -> type-0 notification (append_entity_slot_notification,
1024-B mask). In p2(136) server logs: inbound activity messages were ONLY types 39/47/14 -
NO type 20 ever arrived. The four type=0 pushes were all JOIN grants (t=120025/153483/
236562/254940, body=1024). The request->grant cycle the client is documented to require
has never executed.

### RESULT 2 - THE JOIN GRANT STARVES THE FREE POOL (the arithmetic)
entity_slots.h: kSlotCount = 8192 (1024-byte mask). Defaults: kDefaultServerReserve=256,
kDefaultClientJoinGrant=8192; join_grant() = min(grant, kSlotCount - reserve) = 7936.
prepare_join: serverMask = reserve_high(256); mask = select_free(serverMask, 7936) - the
joining member leases EVERY low slot; only the 256 high reserve slots remain ungranted.
prepare_grant (type-20 path) selects from the complement of held+server slots - i.e. only
those 256 could ever be granted. Against the community doc's figure (client requires
>=4,096 slots still GRANTABLE), 256 < 4,096: the requirement fails by construction, at
JOIN time, before any entity is attempted. Deployed settings.json confirms topology
embedded, server_reserve_count 256, client_join_grant_count unset (default 8192 -> 7936).

### RESULT 3 - THIS UNIFIES THE FRONT'S FACTS (hypothesis, clearly labeled)
Host-only: only the host-side client attempts peer entity creation (20.211 R3).
50x at the transition: per-frame allocate-attempt failing while the free pool is 256.
Entity cluster attached=1 calls=0 even when creation was attempted (20.208 R7/20.210 R3):
creation fails at INDEX ALLOCATION, upstream of the replication codec - the cluster was
never reached, not "the wrong subsystem" (that retirement verdict deserves re-earn).
If the client cannot allocate an index for the peer's player_broadcast entity, it cannot
create it, and there is nothing to replicate to the rig - no peer render, no errors.

server_reserve_count = 0 -> the client LEASES 4,096 and 4,096 remain GRANTABLE.

no-dump and dump modes):

   0xfb403d6a is junk; v1's phantom 4GB mapping let out-of-section writes
   vanish). NEW negative selftest: out-of-span access must fault.

   non-fetch accesses pull the page and resume. PAGE PROVENANCE
   (file|dump|hole) - holes are reported, never silently zero. CRT
   whitelist (memcpy/memset/memmove/strlen/memcmp) emulated in-Python;

svc22 apply decoder (0x1404DC080) executed against dump state with ZERO
scaffolding: .data live values present, registry chain demand-paged from

THE MAP FACT THE ACCEPTANCE EXPOSED: the registry global 0x142439C70
points at heap page 0x18cda4f6000, and dump_healthy_inproc.dmp captured

    mgr 0x46EF040 -> pool 0x1D367478 : 150 free   (second manager, appears at rig join)
    mgr 0x4700E48 -> pool 0x0        :   0 free   (no pool ever attached)
Session fully healthy: peers valid 0x7, players valid 0x3, Citizen join succeeded, 0
checksum failures, peer-creating -> peer-joining -> peer-established.
CONCLUSION: ~145 slots sit free and the client NEVER ASKS. Creation is not reached.
Slot supply was never the blocker. THE ENTITY-INDEX FRONT IS CLOSED.

### RESULT 5 - WHAT THE 44 FAILURES ACTUALLY WERE
Self-allocation during load, in the window before the pool->manager transfer lands. They
have no relation to peers - they fire SOLO and stop once the mask fills. This is the
"flaky gate" that made p2-136/137/138/139 disagree (burst / silent / solo-burst /
silent): a startup race in an unrelated path. 20.212 R3's unification of the front's
facts, 20.213's "slot size gates the attempt", and the whole 20.212-20.218 arc rest on
reading those failures as peer-related. They were not.

### RESULT 6 - RETRACTIONS AND CORRECTIONS
(a) "The host's free-slot mask is EMPTY at Tower entry" (STATE, HANDOFF 2026-08-31,
    20.216-20.218): FALSE as a persistent condition. It is empty only in a brief
    pre-transfer window at load. Every prior boot INFERRED emptiness from idx_alloc
    returning -1; this boot measured the popcount directly (mgr_free=8184/150/145).
(b) 20.217 R2 / STATE: "0x1404FBAD0 = merge into the local mask". WRONG IN KIND -
    0x1404FBAD0 builds {token:4 || bitmap:1024} = 0x404 bytes and SENDS it via the
    common send 0x1404FB770. The sync is an OUTBOUND REPORT, not a fill. The real local
    filler is 0x14170ACB0. 20.218 R2 floated exactly this alternative; it is confirmed.
(c) 20.216 R2: "r9=0x97/0x96 = donated-bit counts". UNFOUNDED - 0x1404F56F0 takes two
    arguments (rcx=pool, rdx=&bitmap); r9 is a leftover register, not a parameter.
(d) MY OWN, THIS SESSION: I reported `pool_assign ret=0x80000001` as a handler failure.
    It is not - the handler returns a BOOL IN AL (`mov al,1` / `xor al,al`); the upper
    RAX bits are undefined. AL=1 = success. Caught by reading before it cost a boot.
(e) MY OWN, THIS SESSION: I reported "pool=0x0 on every probe line - the manager is
    never wired to a pool". FALSE, and it was a bad query, not bad data: I piped through
    `head -20` and the idx_alloc lines (which carry no pool field) filled the window
    before the non-null lines. The managers ARE wired to pools. A truncating pipe is a
    measurement error like any other; the conclusion was published from a view that
    could not have shown the counter-evidence.

## 20.220 *** STATIC (NO BOOT): THE PEER-CREATION LOOP IS FOUND AND READ. ONE PREDICATE
## *** GATES ALLOCATION **ON** AND CREATION **OFF** - AN AUTHORITY SPLIT. AND THE LOOP
## *** USES A DIFFERENT ALLOCATOR THAN THE ONE WE WATCHED FOR EIGHT BOOTS.
## *** (2026-08-31 15:4x, VERIFIED-BY-READING)

### RESULT 1 - THE CREATOR AND ITS CALLERS
`failed to create 'player_broadcast'` fires at caller rva 0x16EE3F7, inside the creator
0x1416EE180 (primary fn 70 B + chained fragment to 0x1416EE3FF). Exhaustive E8/E9 scan of
both .text sections: exactly THREE callers -
  0x140B428D0 (28 B thunk: edx=0)  · 0x140B428F0 (35 B thunk: edx=1, r9=-1)
  0x141308B2A - INSIDE 0x1413086E0 (3001 B) = THE PEER-CREATION LOOP.

### RESULT 2 - THE LOOP, DECODED (0x1413086E0 +0x3A0..+0x44F)
Iterates a collection via 0x14034D130 (next -> rbx = member record). Per element:
  gate 1  0x1412FBA60(&rsp+0x68)                -> false: SKIP
  gate 2  [rdi+0x818] == [rsp+0x68]             -> false: SKIP   (identity match)
  if [rbx+8] == -1:  0x1417040F0(&rsp+0x2c, 2)  -> allocate; -1: skip assign
                     else [rbx+8] = index; 0x141704870(...)
  gate 3  0x1412AADF0()                         -> **TRUE: SKIP**
  if [rbx+8] == -1                              -> SKIP
  gate 4  0x141704400(&rsp+0x28, [rbx+8])       -> [rax] != -1: SKIP (entity exists)
  CREATE 0x1416EE180(&rsp+0x20, edx=2, r8d=[rbx+8], r9d=-1)
So `[rbx+8]` is the PER-MEMBER ENTITY INDEX, and creation needs it VALID.

### RESULT 3 *** THE INVERTED-POLARITY PREDICATE (the structural find) ***
0x1412AADF0() = `0x1412ABCA0() && *0x1412AEE50() != 0`, returns bool.
It appears on BOTH sides of the same decision, with OPPOSITE polarity:
  - allocate wrapper 0x1417040F0: `call 0x1412AADF0; test al,al; JE -> return out=-1`
      => allocates ONLY WHEN THE PREDICATE IS **TRUE**
  - creation loop:                `call 0x1412AADF0; test al,al; JNE -> SKIP`
      => creates   ONLY WHEN THE PREDICATE IS **FALSE**
CONSEQUENCE (VERIFIED-BY-READING): a client can never both allocate an index for a member
and locally create that member's entity. The two modes are mutually exclusive by
construction. INFERRED (labelled): this is an AUTHORITY/ROLE split - the authority
allocates and publishes; the non-authority receives the index and creates locally.
COROLLARY, and this is the lane: for a peer to be created, `[rbx+8]` must ALREADY hold a
valid index that this client did not allocate - i.e. THE INDEX MUST ARRIVE FROM OUTSIDE,
as a per-member field. Nothing in the fork delivers one today.

### RESULT 4 - TWO ALLOCATORS, BOTH ON THE PATH, DOING DIFFERENT JOBS
*** CORRECTED IN-SESSION BEFORE PUBLICATION. The first draft of this result claimed the
creation path never reaches 0x141711D10 and that we had watched the wrong allocator for
eight boots. THAT IS FALSE and was caught by continuing to read instead of stopping at a
satisfying conclusion. The correct reading: ***
  loop 0x1413086E0(+0x44A) -> creator 0x1416EE180 -> 0x14170F190 -> **0x141711D10**
0x14170F190's .pdata entry is 0x14170F190..0x14170F390 and it calls idx_alloc at +0x3E
(0x14170F1CE) - which is exactly the caller_rva=0x170F1D3 mtrace has logged all along.
So there are TWO allocators at TWO different steps:
  (a) the PER-MEMBER INDEX [rbx+8]: loop step 4, via 0x1417040F0 -> 0x140B76E00
      (a small static free-list: bump counter rip+0x143F824 over an array rip+0x1C7955A).
      NOT the pool machinery, and gated by the predicate being TRUE.
  (b) the ENTITY SLOT: inside the create, via 0x14170F190 -> 0x141711D10 (mgr+0xC118),
      the allocator we have hooked since p2-143. Its -1 IS the "failed to create" line.
This STRENGTHENS 20.219 rather than weakening it. Because (b) is on the path, the
paired-window census is a load-bearing inference:
    ZERO idx_alloc calls after the rig joined
      => 0x14170F190 was never called
      => the creator 0x1416EE180 was never called
      => THE LOOP NEVER REACHED ITS CREATE STEP FOR THE PEER.
The loop is being stopped at gates 1-4, or it is not iterating the peer at all. That is
the front, and it is now a statement about GATES, not about slot supply.

### RESULT 5 - THE STATIC WALL, NAMED
0x1412ABCA0 and 0x1412AEE50 both open with the obfuscator's encrypted-global pattern
(`mov rbx,[rip+X]; call 0x1472B4425; xor eax,ebx; call 0x146260781; xor ...`). The
predicate's inputs are not statically resolvable. IT MUST BE MEASURED: a hook on
0x1412AADF0 (37 B, clean 4-byte prologue) logging its return, on BOTH machines, names
which side is authority in one boot. That plus a hook on the loop 0x1413086E0 and on the
creator 0x1416EE180 is the next instrument - and it is small.

### RESULT 6 - WHAT THIS RETIRES AND WHAT IT OPENS
RETIRES: slot SUPPLY as the blocker (20.219, unchanged). The pool/mask machinery IS on
the path - as step (b) - but it has 145 free slots and is never asked, because the loop
stops before the create. Supply was never the question; the GATES are.
OPENS: the per-member entity index `[rbx+8]`. Who writes it, and what wire field is
supposed to carry it? This is the community doc's creation-with-baseline contract
(sections 1.3-1.7) arriving from a completely different direction - the one lead that
has been deprioritised three separate times (20.213 verdict item 1, HANDOFF 2026-08-31
item 4, and again at 20.219).

## 20.221 *** p2-146: GATE 2 IS SOLVED BY MEASUREMENT. THE CREATION LOOP BUILDS ONLY
## *** MEMBERS THE LOCAL PLAYER OWNS; THE PEER'S OWNER FIELD NEVER MATCHES, ON ANY OF
## *** 4,543 OBSERVATIONS. THE LOOP IS NOT THE PEER-RENDERING PATH.
## *** (2026-08-31 16:3x, VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION)

### SETUP
Client DLL 37bfdbd8221f4e7b both machines. Two hooks, BOTH FILTERED to the creation
loop's own call sites (the fix for p2-145's budget being spent by unrelated callers):
  member_get 0x140B39DC0 @caller 0x1308AA9 - logs [ret+0x818]  = gate 2 operand A
  gate1      0x1412FBA60 @caller 0x1308AB6 - OutParam::rcx     = gate 2 operand B
Paired Tower dwell, players valid 0x3. Log 16 MB (the time-based census fix held; p2-145
was 51 MB mac / 155 MB rig). Guard lines (why=not-a-pointer / why=not-a-record): ZERO.

### RESULT 1 - THE COMPARISON, WITH VALUES
Gate 2 is `mov rax,[rdi+0x818]; cmp rax,[rsp+0x68]` (QWORD). Measured:
  operand B (gate1's out-slot) = 0xF5D3535B98AEB768, CONSTANT across all 24 samples
  operand A, by record:
    rec 0x665118D0  owner 0xF5D3535B98AEB768   7,329 samples   *** MATCH -> proceeds ***
    rec 0x665118D0  owner 0x0                  4,543 samples       mismatch
    rec 0x66514EC0  owner 0x846C8338F7D022E6   4,543 samples   *** NEVER MATCHES ***
Two records = two players. Neither identity is the Steam xuid (0x110000130AA9EC5 /
...EC6 in the same log) - they are internal identity handles.

### RESULT 2 - THE RULE, AND WHAT IT MAKES THE LOOP
The loop builds an entity ONLY for a member whose +0x818 owner field equals the local
identity. The local player's record matches and is built. THE PEER'S RECORD CARRIES A
DIFFERENT OWNER AND IS SKIPPED EVERY PASS - 4,543 observations, zero matches. This is
not starvation, not a race, and not a fault we can see from here: it is the loop's own
rule executing as written. CONSEQUENCE: 0x1413086E0 is the LOCAL-PLAYER build path, not
the peer-rendering path. The whole "why doesn't the loop create the peer" framing
(20.220, and this session's p2-145/p2-146 briefs) is answered: it is not supposed to.

### RESULT 3 - WHAT THIS REOPENS, AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT SURVIVES
If peers are not built locally they must ARRIVE. The replication receive cluster
(ent_recv 0x141718510 / ent_header 0x141717EB0 / ent_create 0x141718080) logs ZERO calls
in every boot including this one. It was retired TWICE - 20.210 R3 ("the wrong
subsystem") and re-earned 20.213 R2 ("creation fails upstream of it"). BOTH RATIONALES
ARE NOW SUSPECT: it may log zero because nothing ever sends it a peer entity.
CONSTRAINT THAT STILL HOLDS AND NARROWS THIS (user callout, verified): 20.208 R5 closed
the PEER CHANNEL by pcap - 1,394 packets, largest 268 B, dead flat at co-location -
"the peer does NOT send a packaged guardian". So client<->client pre-packaging stays
REFUTED. Any replication must be SERVER-MEDIATED over the gameplay plane (UDP 30976),
which is exactly 20.209's standing hypothesis and is untouched by any measurement.

### RESULT 4 - THE TWO READINGS, NOT YET SEPARATED (labelled, both live)
 (a) The loop is self-only BY DESIGN; peers arrive by server-mediated replication that
     our fork never sends. Front = the gameplay-plane entity message; the retired
     cluster comes back as the receiver.
 (b) The peer's +0x818 is SUPPOSED to become the local identity under some authority
     hand-off, and the fork never arranges it. Front = what writes +0x818.
DISCRIMINATOR: what writes that field, and whether the peer's record is structurally
complete. Both are offline questions against the p2-146 dump (below).

SHELF LIFE, and it is the reason this dump exists at all: a dump is SCENARIO-SCOPED, not

was taken for) valid only for THIS scenario; a fork change that alters what the client
receives makes it stale. Tier 3 (heap addresses, session ids) snapshot-local.
