### R2 THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT THAT MADE W2 UNREADABLE FOR THE WHOLE SESSION
`gatebit` prints `value=` and I read `value=0` as "the bit is clear" THREE times, including
in a status summary. `value` is the CONTAINER COUNTER; `bitreq` is the derived requirement
(container-at-creation + 6); and the bit itself lives in the word already printed as `mask`.
W2 was measured every boot, under a name that did not say so. Answering it required joining
two probes plus 20.279's "bit 7/6, not 5" - three sources, and it was misread every time.
FIX (shipped, a96a6a70f578fc40): resv_rec now prints `reqA=%u setA=%d reqB=%u setB=%d`.
TWO requirements, not one: p2-170 shows the mac pinning BOTH 6 and 7 from two containers, so
a single global would have answered W2 for whichever container fired last. `set=-1` means
the requirement was not pinned yet - explicitly NOT the same as the bit being clear.
Validated by OFFLINE REPLAY over p2-170's recorded values before deploy; that replay is what
caught the two-container defect.

### R3 *** THE VERDICT: THE BIT IS BIRTH-SET, AND THE TWO POPULATIONS ARE DISJOINT ***
p2-171, both machines, read off one line:
  MAC  rec=0 self   ident=0x00007900A401A8C0  mask=0x0020  reqA=7 setA=0  reqB=6 setB=0
       rec=1 BLANK  ident=0x0000000000000000  mask=0x00C0  reqA=7 setA=1  reqB=6 setB=1
       rec=2 PEER   ident=0xFF000C198801A8C0  mask=0x0020  reqA=7 setA=0  reqB=6 setB=0
              (peer record at EVERY rung 1/1 -> 4/5: setA=0 setB=0, never once set)
  RIG  rec=0        ident=0xFF000C19A401A8C0  mask=0x0040  reqA=6 setA=1   at 1/1 and 2/1
       rec=1        ident=0xFF000C19A401A8C0  mask=0x0000  reqA=6 setA=0   at 3/4
THE RIG LINE IS THE PROOF: the SAME peer identity occupies TWO records simultaneously - one
carrying the required bit and stuck at the bottom of the ladder, one climbing and carrying
none. The populations are disjoint: every record observed with the bit stays at low state;
every record that climbs lacks it.
This is 20.280's "birth-set" clause with its consequence finally read: the bit is stamped at
CREATION from the container the record is born into. It is not granted by claiming, by
climbing, or by the poke - p2-170 ran the guard 1,190 times against a correct card and the
peer's bit never moved off 0.

### R4 WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT OPENS
CLOSES: W2 as "a bit to be set". There is no set-it path. Any plan of the form "make the
guard claim the peer's record so the bit follows" is dead - p2-170 tested exactly that.
CLOSES: the value of further poke boots on this question. The poke opens cond5 and nothing
downstream of cond5 can reach the birth-set bit.
OPENS, and this is the front: WHAT DETERMINES THE CONTAINER A PEER'S RESERVATION RECORD IS
CREATED IN, and can the server influence it? Every fix this session was about a record's
CONTENTS; this is about its CREATION, which is upstream of all of it.
NOT ASSERTED: whether that question is the same as entity construction. Both are creation
questions and they may be one mechanism seen from two sides, but nothing measured says so.
The next session should scope CREATION (record + entity) rather than assume a boundary.

## 20.287 *** THE BIRTH-SET FRAMING IS CORRECTED: THE REQUIRED BIT IS OR-ACCUMULATED AT
## *** CLAIM TIME, NOT FIXED AT BIRTH. THE PEER'S RECORD IS ONE CLAIM UNDER A LIVE
## *** CONTAINER AWAY FROM PASSING THE GUARD. THE WALL IS THAT NO 0/1-CONTAINER CLAIM
## *** EVER PROCESSES THE PEER'S IDENTITY - AND THE MASKS GATING THAT CLAIM HAVE NO
## *** COMPUTED WRITER IN THE CLIENT: THEY ARRIVE AS A MESSAGE-DELIVERED IMAGE. THE
## *** SERVER LEVER IS "DELIVER THE PARTICIPANT IMAGE", NOT "INFLUENCE THE CONTAINER".
## *** (2026-09-03 20:14 PDT, static VERIFIED-BY-READING + logq replay over p2171; NO BOOT) ***

### R0 CORRECTION TO 20.286's "BIRTH-SET" (retraction-class; read before building on 20.286)
The bit the guard requires is stamped by an OR at every claim, so a record's word
ACCUMULATES container bits across its life. The only writers of the word (rec+0x3112):
  - record ctor 0x1417BF040 zeroes it (0x1417bf069, xor edi,edi - VERIFIED firsthand, the
    "zeroes the extras" claim of 20.280 stands);
  - the claim's OR: 0x1417C08F0 @ 0x1417c0ea6 `or word ptr [rdx + rsi + 0x3112], r15w`
    (r15w = 1 << edx, edx = the claim's bit argument). A [base+index*scale+disp] SIB form -
    INVISIBLE to field_xref disp32 scans, which is why every earlier scan found "no setter"
    (20.280 R2's "cursor/computed" guess; the mechanism is now named);
  - the initial word content arrives by SSE copy from the claim's 4th argument
    (0x1417c0c71/c75 `movups xmm0,[rdi+0x20]; movups [rbx+0x3112],xmm0` - same blind spot);
  - the disown 0x1417C4810 clears (already on record).
IN-VIVO PROOF OF ACCUMULATION: mac rec=1 (blank) went 0x0080 -> 0x00C0 between t=147325 and
t=241632 in p2-171 - a record carrying container-1's bit GAINED container-0's bit (logq over
p2171.db). 20.286 R3's "populations are disjoint" observation STANDS, but its mechanism
reading ("stamped at creation from the container") is superseded: records are disjoint
because the 0/1 claims never process the peer's identity, not because the bit is birth-locked.

### R1 THE COMPLETE CLAIM-PATH CENSUS (all six callers of 0x1417C08F0/0x1417C3480)
Two container-id fields feed every claim:
  A. dword[C+8] where C = [X+8], X = MGR+0x30 (MGR = the session manager whose +0x270 is
     the entity-index orchestrator; X's layout: {+0: pool, +8: C, +0x10: reservation mgr,
     +0x18: table counter, +0x1c: maskA copy, +0x28: self idx, +0x2c: slot snapshot}):
     +6 applied AT USE, by the sweep AND the guard (0x1417024b4 and 0x141703910 both).
  B. dword[obj+0x850], passed RAW, by ALL FOUR join/reserve-family claims
     (0x141769402, 0x141769811, 0x141770e29, 0x1417b8edd - the first is inside RESERVE
     0x141769230, the 20.271 join-gate chain). Presumably pre-derived (id+6); its writers
     are three `mov dword [reg+0x850],0` in the obfuscated 0x1488xxxxx family (field_xref).
The guard's requirement uses field A; the peer's record carries bit 5 = id -1 + 6, so the
ONLY claimer that ever touched it used container -1 (the flicker 0x0020<->0x0000 on
rec=0/rec=2 in p2-171 = repeated disown + re-claim under -1).

### R2 WHY THE 0/1 CLAIMS NEVER REACH THE PEER: THE SWEEP'S THREE GATES
The sweep 0x1417021C0's claim loop, per participant i (VERIFIED instruction by instruction):
  1. maskB bit i (iteration: 0x1404df480 returns lowest set bit of dword[table+0x5924C],
     0x1404df4b0 clears it - the loop IS the mask);
  2. maskA bit i (0x1404df640: `mov eax,[rcx+0x59248]; shr eax,cl` - table = pool+0x6C38);
  3. the gate byte (0x1404dd470 - the cond5 byte p2-170 poked);
  then claim under edx = dword[C+8]+6 (0x1417024cd -> 0x1417C3480 -> 0x1417C08F0).
The disown pass (pass 1) iterates RECORDS by bit and disowns any record no slot's 86-byte
blob claims - as mapped in 20.280; now anchored to its exact loop.

### R3 THE MASKS HAVE NO COMPUTED WRITER - THEY ARRIVE AS AN IMAGE (the lever)
maskA = dword[pool+0x6C38+0x59248], maskB = dword[...+0x5924C]. Field_xref on 0x59248,
0x5924C, and the pool-relative aliases 0x5FE80/0x5FE84: ZERO disp32 writes, zero leas -
readers only. The participant table is born ALL-ZERO including the masks (table ctor
0x1404DD1A0: memset 0x59260 + 32 row ctors + 64-entry side array at +0x55808). The wholesale
copier 0x1403CB340 re-read firsthand: call 1 backs the table up to the stack, call 2 copies
TABLE -> staging buffer (publish; 20.253's correction CONFIRMED), tail virtual calls
[rax+0x100] on the global 0x142935F10 singleton - WHICH IS NULL in dump_p2146 (so that
apply is inert in the healthy session). Copier call sites: the pool ctor + one gap thunk.
THE APPLY CANDIDATE: 0x1416E73A0 (0 direct callers = dispatched) takes a descriptor
{+[0],[1]: registry key, +8: IMAGE POINTER, +0x18: byte}, resolves an object via
0x140c23220 (the obfuscated registry wall), stamps obj+0x111E9 = 1 ("arrived") + the byte
at obj+0x111E8, and tail-jmps 0x1403CB720 which CACHES the image pointer at obj+0x10EB0.
Later, 0x1403CD4C0 fires (predicate 0x140dd5b70 on obj+0x10EB0) and applies the cached
image via 0x1404da970 into obj+0x28. This is 20.253 R4's "later apply path writes the
table directly" - now WITH its shape: message descriptor -> cached image -> wholesale apply.
The fork has proven it can deliver bodies to the message layer (type-45, p2-154).

### R4 THE REFRAME (supersedes the 20.286 "THE ONE QUESTION")
Old question: "what determines the container a peer's record is created in?" - answered:
the container of whichever claim path processes the identity, and that is CHOICELESS for
the peer because only the -1 path ever sees it. New question: **can the fork deliver the
participant image (or the fields feeding it) so the sweep's claim arms for the peer's slot
under a live container?** If yes: the OR stamps bit 6/7 onto the peer's record on the next
sweep, the guard's requirement is satisfied, the claim effect persists, the disown stops.
This makes the next boot an IMPLEMENTATION test, not an exploration.

### R1 THE OBJECT THAT CACHES THE IMAGE IS THE POOL-ADJACENT TABLE-HEADER FAMILY
field_xref 0x10EB0: 75 accesses; the on-family cluster sits at 0x1403C8xx-0x1403CDxx
(0x1403cb72b WRITE = the setter; 0x1403c80e8/0x1403cce1d/0x1403cd4de/0x1403cd64f reads with
`lea [img+0x28]`-style follow-ups). Same neighborhood as 0x1403c9fb0, which receives
pool+0x6C30 and constructs THE PARTICIPANT TABLE at +8 (0x1404DD1A0). So the image hangs
off the pool's table-header object: image ptr at TH+0x10EB0, arrived flag at TH+0x111E9,
keyed apply into TH+0x28 (0x1403CD4C0 -> 0x1404DA970).
THE AUTHORITY SPLIT AT THE READ SITE (0x141703D70, VERIFIED): authority (0x1412aadf0) ->
read live object (0x1416fe700); NON-authority -> read FROM the cached image
(0x1416fcca0(image) -> 0x1404f4830). The 20.220/20.253 authority predicate decides whether
a client reads live state or the delivered image. This is the sharing layer.

### R2 THE REGISTRY RESOLUTION MECHANICS (and the wall, evidenced)
0x140c23220(key0,key1): gate chain 0x140e36c30 (flattened, global 0x1427B2210) + 0x140c21370
-> manager getter 0x140c21fe0 -> dword table [mgr + (key0+key1*2)*4] -> entry -> handle dword
[mgr + ent*8 + 0x14] -> object via 0x1403c9450 (handle-pool: base qword@0x141BFAFF8 +
(idx & 0x1FFF) * stride dword@0x141BFB000).
FEMU RESULT: the flattened getters RETURN but yield the ENCRYPTED handle (e.g.
0xeca98714782985e3); the subsequent dereference faults read-beyond-image. The encrypted

## 20.291 THE IMAGE FRONT'S PREMISE DOES NOT SURVIVE READING (2026-09-03 ~23:05)
## *** THE IMAGE FRONT'S PREMISE DOES NOT SURVIVE READING. THE "MASKS ARRIVE AS A

### R0 THE HEADLINE
The front as stated in STATE/20.287/20.288 ("can the fork deliver the participant image so
the sweep's claim arms for the peer's slot?") rests on one link: that the delivered image
carries the maskA/maskB projection. That link has NO evidence. Its stated evidence
(participant-image-format-spec.md 2) is a misread of a non-instruction boundary, and an
independent structural check rules out the direct form. The front should not be booted as
an implementation test. The masks' "no computed writer" fact is UNAFFECTED and re-derived
here independently (R8) - what dies is the story about how they WOULD be written.

### R1 RETRACTION OF 20.288 R3: THE IMAGE HANDLER IS NOT UNREFERENCED
20.288 R3: "0x1416E73A0 has ZERO references of any kind ... no qword/dword pointer anywhere
in the image (binary search)" -> the dispatcher "lives behind the obfuscator. DO NOT chase
it statically." THE POINTER IS IN THE STATIC FILE at offset 0x1C9E308. The search looked
for 0x1416E73A0; destiny2_unpacked_full.exe stores RUNTIME-RELOCATED pointers (stale base
0x7FF6AF7F0000), so the stored qword reads 0x7FF6B0ED73A0. This is the exact trap
documented in TOOLS.md for dump_search.py and the same class as 20.209 R2. METHOD NOTE: the
find took ~20 s - `dump_search.py --u64 <dump-base + rva>` on dump_p2146, one hit.

### R2 THE TABLE (VERIFIED-BY-READING, static + dump agree)
Static 0x141C9F698, 19 entries, stride 24: {describe_fn, predicate, handler}.
  - predicate is the SAME value in all 19 entries: 0x140E0DC10 = `xor al,al; ret` (false).
  - the image handler 0x1416E73A0 is ENTRY 4; its describe_fn is 0x1416E6200.
  - the cluster 20.288 flagged for hooking is entries 0/1/3/6 (0x1416e7240 / 7340 / 7370 /
    72d0). Nothing here is a per-message TYPE index yet - see R5.
0x1416E6200 is a DESCRIBE/trace function, not a parser: it reads {len @+4, ptr @+8} off the
message and formats a name via 0x140412a40. The "decode scratch" strings name that role.

### R3 THE IMAGE HANDLER, END TO END - AND WHY THE FORK CANNOT SEND IT
0x1416E73A0(rdx = msg):
    ecx = msg[0x00] (byte)          ; key0
    edx = msg[0x01] (byte)          ; key1
    obj = 0x140C23220(key0, key1)   ; registry; index = key0 + key1*2 (VERIFIED at
                                    ; 0x140c2324f `lea rdx,[rsi+rdi*2]`), tail
                                    ; `call 0x1403C9450` = the handle pool
    if !obj: return
    obj[0x111E8] = msg[0x18] (byte) ; generation/slot tag
    obj[0x111E9] = 1                ; "arrived"
    jmp 0x1403CB720(obj, msg[0x08], msg[0x10])
msg+0x08 and msg+0x10 are POINTERS. A message carrying raw process pointers is an
IN-PROCESS QUEUE EVENT, not a wire body - consistent with the plane's own name
(simulation_queue_*). THE FORK CANNOT EMIT THIS MESSAGE. Any delivery must come from
upstream code that allocates the buffers and posts the event.

### R4 NEW ASSET: THE BAP QUEUE-EVENT PLANE AND ITS WIRE FORMAT
The naming strings sit immediately after the table at 0x141C9F870+:
  simulation_queue_bap_message_queue_event_apply
  simulation_queue_bap_message_queue_response_event_apply decode scratch
  simulation_queue_bap_push_event_insert encode scratch
  simulation_queue_bap_push_event_apply
  simulation_queue_activity_client_membership_insert::payload
They are lea-referenced by QUEUE-EVENT ROUTER ARMS 0x11/0x12/0x13 (0x1416F0F82 ->
0x141C9F870; 0x1416F1342; 0x1416F1939) - i.e. the arms 20.288/router_arm_table already
mapped. ARM 0x11 (0x1416F0F60) IS THE WIRE DECODER (VERIFIED, full read):
    alloc 0x80098-byte block (0x140374340, named by the string above)
    bit-reader over the wire body {ptr = arg+0x08, len = arg+0x04}   (0x140351d90)
    memset(block, 0, 0x80098)
    read 32 bits -> block+0x00        (0x1403513b0 = read_bits)
    read 32 bits -> block+0x04
    read 32 bits -> block+0x08
    read 32 bits -> block+0x0C  = count
    read (count*8) bits -> block+0x10        ; = count BYTES of payload
    read 0x440 bits      -> block+0x80010    ; = 136-byte trailer
    if reader-ok (0x14034e9b0): 0x140E04E30(block)   ; POST to the queue
This is a server->client injection point into the client's own simulation work queue, on a
transport THE FORK ALREADY SPEAKS. Recorded as a CAPABILITY. It is NOT a road to a rendered
peer on current evidence (R0/R3/R7) and no boot should be spent on it yet.

### R5 THE POSTER IS GENUINELY OBFUSCATED (20.288's wall, relocated to the right place)
0x140E04E30 is control-flow-flattened with encrypted state (calls into 0x144F9D1FB /
0x146260781 / 0x1472B4425; constant-compare dispatch on 0xF776133 / 0x29ED08E6 / ...).
So the WIRE is readable and the QUEUE'S INTERNAL ROUTING is not. Which of the 19 handlers a
posted event reaches is NOT statically determinable. 20.288 R3's conclusion was right about
a wall and wrong about where it stands.

### R6 RETRACTION: participant-image-format-spec.md 2 IS NOT SUPPORTED
The spec's mask link is: "the per-entry processor immediately loads ebx = 0x6c38 (mov
ebx,0x6c38 @ 0x1404f4754)". THAT INSTRUCTION DOES NOT EXIST. Census of the WHOLE image:
exactly TWO immediate loads of 0x6c38 in executable sections -
    0x1404F728A  lea r15,[r14+0x6c38]  (the POOL CONSTRUCTOR - see R8)
    0x14707277E  mov eax,0x6c38        (inside the obfuscated region)
Neither is at 0x1404f4754, and `0x6c38` appears NOWHERE in 0x1404F4700..0x1404F482C.
CAUSE: 0x1404F4740 is NOT a function start - .pdata gives 0x1404F4700..0x1404F482C, so
0x1404F4740 is +0x40 INTO it; disassembling from a non-instruction boundary yields a
plausible-looking but false instruction stream. The spec's render-side citation has the
same defect: it attributes `imul 0x20 @ 0x1404f4ac3` to function 0x1404f4830, but .pdata
puts 0x1404F4830..0x1404F4975 and 0x1404F4A10..0x1404F4E47 in DIFFERENT functions.
The true 0x1404F4700 is a 0x400-byte record copy (8 x 0x80 movups) - no mask reference.
LESSON (already ours, violated again): resolve EVERY address through pdata_bounds.py before
disassembling it. This is the READING-THE-INSTRUMENT shape at one remove - a conclusion
drawn from a disassembly without first checking the disassembly was anchored.

### R7 THE STRUCTURAL CONTRADICTION (the decisive argument)
The object the image handler writes is a HANDLE-POOL entry: 0x140C23220 tails into
0x1403C9450, which computes `base@0x141F8AFF8 + (idx & 0x1FFF) * stride@0x141F8B000`.
Read from dump_p2146 (VERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION of the read): base = 0x234038BBC80,
STRIDE = 0x19540 = 103,744 bytes. The handler's fields 0x10EB0 / 0x111E8 / 0x111E9 all fit.
The masks do NOT. maskA/maskB are at +0x59248/+0x5924C of the participant-table object that
0x1404DD1A0 allocates and clears: `memset(obj, 0, 0x59260)` = 365,152 bytes, then 32
sub-objects at stride 0x2AC0 from +0x38, then a ctor at +0x59220.
  365,128  >  103,744.  The image-receiving object cannot contain the masks.
STATED LIMIT (do not overclaim): the applier 0x1404DA970 hands the image to a virtual call
[dest+0x818]+0x18 where dest = &TH[0x28]. If that resolver holds a pointer to the
participant table, an INDIRECT write is not excluded. Nothing evidences one, and it is not
what the front was built on - but it is the one falsifier of R7 and it is cheap to check.

Confirmed WITHOUT relying on any prior entry:
  - BIRTH: 0x1404DD1A0 memsets the whole 0x59260 object to zero. "Born zero" = VERIFIED.
  - ACCESS CENSUS (immediate/disp32 sweep of .text for 0x59248/0x5924C/0x59250): 6 sites -

So "no computed writer in the client" STANDS on its own evidence. Remaining candidates for

The entity-receiver chain (five-condition gate, maskA/maskB, cond5) has NEVER been observed

necessarily undated, only un-locatable by the current patterns.

have otherwise fired correctly all session (POSTMORTEM 09-03's own finding); this is the

User: "you're likely looking at the wrong thing and the bit isn't the gate but lets

### R1 THE CONSTANTS ARE SOUND (the corpus checks out)
Independently verified against the binary, both getters are exactly as documented:
  0x1404DD470  imul rdx,rax,0x2ac0 / movzx eax,byte [rdx+rcx+0x38] / shr al,4 / and al,1
               -> stride 0x2AC0, offset +0x38, bit 4. ALL THREE CONFIRMED.
  0x1404DF470  mov eax,[rcx+0x59248] -> maskA at +0x59248. CONFIRMED.
Neither is a .pdata function start (both sit in gaps - small leaf getters), so they were
read with the LINEAR disassembler, not disasm_fn (which would have invented a stream).

### R2 *** THE COND5 BIT IS NOT THE CREATION GATE ***
Scanned both .text sections for the 0x2AC0 record stride: 59 hits, ~10 genuine
record-indexing sites (the 0x140726xxx cluster is `cmp dword [rsp+0x2AC0]`, stack noise).
EVERY genuine site is a READ or an address computation. NONE writes +0x38.
Decisive: callers.py on 0x1404DD470 gives TWO call sites, both inside
0x141702580/0x1417021C0 - and that function also calls 0x1416E9CF0, 0x1416E9E50 and
0x1416CACD0, i.e. it is the RECONCILE/RELEASE SWEEP (20.296's family), not creation.
The control flow is real - cond5 clear DOES skip the guard:
  0x14170266e call 0x1404dd470 / test al,al / jne 0x1417026f1
  0x141702677 xor r13b,r13b / jmp 0x14170273c   <- bit clear: SKIP the guard entirely
  0x141702728 call 0x141703910                  <- the guard, only on the bit-set path
BUT the creation loop 0x1413086E0 NEVER CALLS 0x1404DD470 AT ALL. Its call census:
member_get 0x140B39DC0, gate1 0x1412FBA60, memidx_alloc 0x1417040F0, idx_publish
0x141704870, already-created 0x141704400, pb_create 0x1416EE180 - and no cond5 reader,
no maskA getter. So cond5 gates a claim inside the SWEEP; it has nothing to do with
whether a body is built.

  0x141308aa4 call member_get           -> rdi = the member record
  0x141308ab1 call gate1(&[rsp+0x68])   -> fills a stack slot, returns al

  0x141308ac1 cmp rax,[rsp+0x68]        -> *** GATE 2 *** ; sete/test/je skip

`grep` in the Claude Code shell is a FUNCTION that routes to ugrep with
`--ignore-files` (honours .gitignore) and `-I` (skips files it guesses are binary):
  - .gitignore:13-14 excludes RE_build/ AND RE_output/ - THE ENTIRE SOURCE TREE AND
    THE ENTIRE EVIDENCE CORPUS are invisible to any recursive grep.
  - the capture logs are misdetected as binary (`file` calls server.log a "core file
    (Xenix)"), so /usr/bin/grep -c peer returns 95 and the wrapped grep returns
    NOTHING - silently, exit 0.
It produced two false claims here before it was caught (a "the knob is not in the
repo" miss, and "the 20.53 capture has no variant= lines" - it has 53). Use
/usr/bin/grep for anything under RE_build/ or RE_output/. RE_scripts/loggrep.sh calls
bare `grep -an` and INHERITS THIS.

CANNOT catch a claim whose search TOOL was silently blind. New class, not yet covered.

Cap 2 -> 10 was applied and CONFIRMED LOADED by the server's own startup echo

session runs dry thereafter. Cap 0 (unlimited) is NOT the answer either - republish is
~5 s, so a ten-minute dwell is ~120 bodies, the 127/146 range that blocked the Tower
load at p2(111). THE REAL FIX is to clear `peerWithdrawn` on acknowledgement (one line,
activity_membership_push.cpp:384's block) - a REBUILD, so it is a decision, not a flip.

Two launches were lost to environment, not code. The user forced ethernet, which
retired the mac's WiFi address 192.168.1.164 - the address the server was BOUND to.
Six config fields pointed at it (4 server, mac client host, rig client host+config_url)
plus THREE hardcoded copies in tooling (reset_lobby_claims.sh, deploy_p2d6_gameplay.sh
x2). All repointed to 192.168.1.7; the tooling now DERIVES the host from settings.json
so it cannot rot again. SELF-INFLICTED, RECORDED: I rewrote the rig's settings.json
with PowerShell `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which emits a BOM (EF BB BF); the shim
would not parse it and the rig threw "problem verifying game files' integrity". Fixed
by rewriting from the backup with UTF8Encoding($false). RULE: never write a config on
the rig with Set-Content -Encoding UTF8; use [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText with an
explicit no-BOM encoding, and verify byte 0 == 123.

### R2 THE INSTALLER REFRAMED (correction of 20.251 R1's framing)
0x1416CACD0 (1777 B, obfuscator-flattened) is the function that STORES the four receive-
interface vptrs into an object ([obj+0xA8]=0x141C9ADD8 ent_recv's, +0x100=0x141C9AE50,

installer". BOTH are defective framings: its four callers are ALL mask-driven
reconcile/release paths, i.e. it runs on entities as they pass through the
participant-table lifecycle:

  0x1416FFE55 - the same family, 27-B check of [+0x44]/[+0x48] lifecycle bytes
  0x1417026D3 - THE CLAIM SWEEP ITSELF (anchor 0x1404F5800 -> +0x6C38 table ->

              0x1404DF480/0x1404DF500/0x1404DF600) with CACD0 deep in its release arm
  0x141709D96 - the reconciler: for each mask bit (32-entry scan) match the entity,
              release + CACD0 - and its primary 0x141709B10 reads the SAME anchor and
              maskA getter (20.292's container/table map)
THE REFRAME: the receive interfaces are installed by the MASK LIFECYCLE - an entity
passing through the participant-table reconcile/release machinery gets (re)configured
with the receive vptrs. 20.223's zero instances are CONSISTENT: in the p2-146 dump no
participant transition had ever occurred (both players present the whole session), so

### R1 THE FAMILY IS FOUR RECEIVE INTERFACES, ALL AT VTABLE SLOT 10 (extends 20.222 R4)
One class table at 0x141C9AD90 (73 entries). The ctor 0x1416BB1E0 (re-read; its four
lea targets ARE the four secondary vptrs) stores four blocks: obj+0xA8/0x100/0x140/
0x1680. ALL FOUR slot-10 (+0x50) handlers decoded:

  B 0x141718AE0            455 B - kind-typed list (kinds <= 0x15, 0xA0 payloads)
  C 0x1417183C0            333 B - index-typed list (indexes <= 0x1f)
  D 0x141718CB0             54 B - ONE schema-walked blob (walker 0x1404C74B0, packed
                                    key in the global at 0x14206AF20, 0xD0 object)
B and C write the SAME 0x84-stride records ent_recv writes. All four report errors
through the owner's vtable+0x60 with a code (1 = alloc fail, 3 = decode fail).

### R2 THE BIT READER IS FEMU-VALIDATED (the encoder's first duty)
Reader state: {+0 base, +8 end, +0x10 size, +0x24 total bits, +0x28 64-bit window,
+0x30 consumed-in-window, +0x38 next-refill cursor}. The bit = MSB of the window
(test 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, shift LEFT); refills byte-swap the next u64. WIRE =
MSB-FIRST BITS IN BIG-ENDIAN 64-BIT WORDS. Primitives: 0x140350EF0 (1 bit),
0x1403513B0 (N bits), 0x140351F70 (skip N). Oracle: alternating 80-bit pattern and
BITN(16)=0xBEEF reproduced exactly.
TRAP RETIRED: disasm_fn.py's "protobuf tag" annotations are a HEURISTIC MISNOMER on
this cluster - `mov edx,8` is an 8-bit READ WIDTH, not a wire tag. (TOOLS.md's line
34 heuristic nearly re-taught me protobuf; the femu run proved bit-widths.)

### R3 ent_header 0x141717EB0 IS BIT-EXACT VALIDATED (femu A/B, single-bit runs)
Wire order: bit A (1 = empty-header path; 0 = five presence bits follow); the five
bits map to record+0x40 mask bits 0,1,2,3,6 EMPIRICALLY (B->0x01, C->0x02, D->0x04,
E->0x08, F->0x40 - each isolated in its own run); mask bit6 -> the anchor codec into
record+0x0c; then bit G (0 -> record+2 word = arg5; 1 -> bit H: 0 -> 0xFFFF; 1 ->
read8 - femu reproduced 0xA8 and 0x14 exactly); 0x1416BAB50(scratch, word); if
(mask&5)==4 (destroy set, create clear) a 16-bit signed read becomes ent_create's
5th arg. Tail-call ent_create(mgr, reader, record, arg3, that word).

### R4 THE ANCHOR CODEC 0x1404C16C0 IS FULLY DECODED (it is the "entity_index" codec)
value13 = read13; salt4 = read4; unvalidated: high2 = read2; validated (the
r9b=1 form ent_header uses): high2 comes from a CONTEXT GLOBAL, gated by the
byte at 0x1420BFD91 and the dword compare against -2/-1 -> dst = 0xFFFFFFFF on
invalid. Compose: ((high2<<4|salt4)<<16)|value13 = a 22-bit handle. femu confirmed
consumption: absent = 1 bit; present+validated = 17 bits; my synthetic payloads all
validated to -1 (the context global in the dump is in the invalid state - OPEN).

### R5 ent_create 0x141718080 (the consumer), statically complete:
id = record+8; validate (lease bitmap mgr+0xc520 bit; mgr+0x114 word -> table A
descriptor 0x1430B0440; descriptor+8 == id). mask bit0 (create): rec+0x44 = read8,
rec+0 (kind) = read2, codecObj = 0x1416EAE90([mgr+0x10], kind), size ->
rec+0x2c, alloc -> rec+0x30, payload via codec vtbl+0x60, or vtbl+0x18 -> rec+0x2e.
bit0 clear + descriptor: copy DEFAULTS from the descriptor (kind, +0x2c/+0x2e/
+0x30/+0x04) - the descriptor IS the default entity. bit1: second buffer rec+0x38
(descriptor template at desc+0x38, or decoded via 0x14170B600), then the APPLY at
codec vtbl+0x70. bit2: one presence bit -> rec+0x46. femu reached the pool chain
and died on a dump hole ("no dump page", RIP in 0x1416CBBxx) - header tier exact,
payload tier classified as dump-limited, not hidden.

not hold them). From the dump: table A entries 0..6 live (7+ = 0xFF/0xFE empty

R1 THE HANG IS IN THE SECOND LANDING, AND ALL THREE HANGING RIGS LANDED THE
FIRST ONE. Every boot's rig: first landing (fade_release result=ok) at t~6.5s,
then composition zeroed (the PEER ROW'S ARRIVAL - the client clears and
rebuilds on composition change, L8's own design) -> join_ready forced ->
owner_slot forced -> region native -> [should: fade_release ISSUED].
p2-175's rig issued it 11.8s after its last engagement. The three hanging
rigs NEVER issue it.

R2 THE DELTA, MEASURED:
    p2-175 (LAND, cap=2): 2 peer bodies, then permanent withdrawal. The rig
      engaged the mac's record in a 20-hit, 219ms BURST (t=116250-116469),
      then only its own record. Landing issued 1.9s after the burst ended.
    p2-176 (HANG, cap=10): 101 included bodies over 390s, ~5s median gap,
      withdrawals at 248s/337s with the flow RESUMING after each (4 sessions
      x cap each). Rig engaged the mac's record 25,871 times from t=90156 -
      15ms BEFORE its second region-native (t=90171).
    p2-178 (HANG): 46 bodies, bursts of ~7/10s (~1.4s gaps). Rig flood
      77,021 hits, first at t=74453 - 16ms before region-native (t=74469).
    p2-179 (HANG): 54 bodies, same burst shape. Rig flood 17,802 hits,
      first t=66563 - 15ms before region-native (t=66578). The flood ran
      255s; the rig got a THIRD region-native at t=324172 (3s after the
      flood stopped) and STILL never issued fade_release.
  THE 15-16ms PRECESSION IS CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL THREE: the peer record's
  arrival/engagement IS the thing happening at the re-entry moment.

R3 THE MECHANISM (upgrades H-land's churn wording): each peer-row-driven
composition change resets the client's re-landing; the landing completes
only after a QUIET WINDOW (~12-18s) with no further change. At body cadence
the changes never stop, so fade_release never issues, the loading loop runs
until the transport/join eventually errors. A brief engagement (20 hits,
withdrawn fast) clears and the landing completes - which is why the FAST
withdrawal of cap=2 lands and the sustained row of cap=10 hangs.

      include the peer row at most once every ~30s. Between inclusions the
      composition is stable for >12s, so each re-landing completes. The row
      is then SUSTAINED at 30s cadence - what the replication/transition
      front needs. ~10 lines in session_messages.cpp, settings-gated, default

      the client churned the entire time, so stable-presence at body cadence

## 20.325 *** THE TYPE-20 BODY DECODE FIX (FEMU LANES, NO BOOT): the encoder was ***
## *** wrong two ways; both fixed and validated bit-identical to the positive control ***

R1 THE LANE'S VERDICT (femu_type20_body_validation.md): the fork's type-20 body
did NOT decode - the client's schema walker consumed 15 of 14584 bits (empty

full decoder 0x1404D92A0 reads before the schema (its flag bit, then the
resolver's schema gate) - without them the BLOCK-A count reads 0 and the decode
collapses; (2) BLOCK B wrote ONE presence bit per element where schema node
0x80809446 (pmap 320 = 64 x 5) wants FIVE field-presence bits per element
(id, sub, sub0, sub1, sub2) - 251 bits short.

R2 THE CAVEAT THAT RECONCILES WITH p2-198: fixing the body makes it DECODE, not
ALLOCATE - the decoder's return ignores schema content (claim J's "silent
success"), and the MASK filled in p2-198 because the TYPE-20 ARRIVAL triggers
the entity-manager init (CLAIM I's chain), not because the body decoded. The
mask gain (0 -> 144-150) came from the arrival; the body content is what the
4096x0x20 table build consumes - which is the system the downstream chain (the
client's belief about ITS allocation) reads. Both matter; they are different.

R3 THE FIX (applied to activity_entity_index_allocation_encoder.cpp): (1) two
leading 1-bits at the top of encode(); (2) BLOCK B per-element: drop the outer
single present/absent bit - the populated row's own leading "id present" bit is
the first of its five, empty rows write five 0-bits. New body = 1854 bytes
(the lane's predicted size exactly).

R4 THE VALIDATION: the lane's resolver harness (0x1404C72E0 with the registry
graft it documented) on the GATE-ALIGNED body (the harness's input starts at
the gate bit - the full decoder consumes the flag bit itself, so the faithful
arm is "drop the flag, feed the rest as-is"): consumed 14640/14832, out
00 01 00 00 ff... - BIT-IDENTICAL to the lane's positive control (which carries
the documented end-fault in BOTH runs - the walker's own tail behavior, not a
body defect). The old body's arms never matched the control under any leading-
bit offset; the fixed body matches exactly under the correct alignment.

R5 DEPLOYMENT: the fixed encoder is built into the next server deploy. p2-199's
live server still carries the old body (the mask gain is arrival-driven and
persists); the next boot's type-20 pushes decode FOR CONTENT for the first
time. Harness geometry note for future lanes: the resolver harness's input
must start at the GATE bit (drop the decoder's flag bit first) - the three
leading-bit sweep arms all misalign otherwise.

## 20.326 *** STATIC (NO BOOT): THE VIEW MESSAGE IS STRUCTURALLY DROPPED - NO ***
## *** SWITCH CASE, NO APPLY SLOT. ROW 6C'S TWO SUSPECTS ARE MOOT AT THIS LAYER. ***

R1 THE RELIABLE-MESSAGE REGISTRY IS FULLY DECODED (dump_p2146 runtime base
0x7FF756D00000): 45 entries, stride 0x40, base 0x23345E021D8 (entry id k at
base + k*0x40; the view = base + 0xA00 exactly). Entry = 8 qwords: [present,
name-ptr, (u32 0, u32 min), u32 max, encode, decode, h0, h1]. The live

R2 THE DISPATCHER (registry vtable slot 0 = 0x1416E2A90; ZERO direct callers -
virtual-only entry) decodes the record framing: [6-bit id][18-bit declared
size]; refuses id > 0x2C (44); indexes entries + id*0x40; length-gates
declared-size in [entry+0x14, entry+0x18]; absent entry or failed gate =

(rcx = registry ctx +0x20 object, r9 = id, [rsp+0x20] = declared size,
[rsp+0x28] = &decoded struct). The decoded struct then flows into the same
switch 20.319 mapped - this dispatcher is the bridge between the reliable
queue and the connection-layer switch.

R3 THE VERDICT: case 40 (view-establishment) -> jump-table slot 16 ->
0x1416E0A40 = a bare `ret` - SILENT DROP. Read from the actual tables in the
static image (byte table 0x1416E0A88[id] -> slot; dword table 0x1416E0A44[slot]
-> offset from image base 0x14000000). CROSS-VALIDATED FOUR WAYS: id 10 ->
0x1416E0460 (the join gate, 20.319's record exactly); id 11 -> 0x1416E0E10
(peer-connect, same); ids 12/38 -> the same bare-ret stub 20.319 already

R4 THE TWO-PLANE CONSUMPTION RULE: exactly FIVE messages carry h0 apply slots

## 20.327 *** LANE A (STATIC): THE TYPE-9 DESIGNATION IS STRUCTURALLY DEAD - THE ***
## *** CLIENT NEVER READS ANY BODY FIELD AS THE SESSION KEY. THE NO-OP WAS A ***
## *** CLIENT-LOCAL STATE MISS, NOT AN IDENTITY MISMATCH. ***

R1 0x140E36C30 (the "unmix") is a PURE GETTER that decodes the encoded pointer
at DAT_14280E210 (two VMP cookie thunks) and returns the managed-session slot
array or null. IT IGNORES ITS ARGUMENT - the caller's body (rcx) is never
read.

R2 DAT_14280E210 is POPULATED in our sessions (encoded pointer 0x2BEC2E542AC0
7326, nonzero): it is the 0x2D0=720-stride managed-session array the
ms-start-gate lane already mapped. The table is NOT empty.

R3 THE KEY FIELD is slot +0x2958 (u32 member/machine-id, -1 = empty), assigned
BY THE CLIENT during managed-session setup, resolved via 0x1403c6810 (VMP) -
NOT derived by XOR from the activity soid (the handbook's XOR stride belongs
to the membership plane, not this table).

R4 THE DECISIVE FINDING: in 0x140C02690, the type-9 body's qword[body+1] is
stored to [rsp+0x10] at entry and NEVER RE-READ. The active slot is selected
from a CLIENT-LOCAL INDEX (first dword of the DAT_1427F46E8 encoded-ptr
record), not from any wire id. VERDICT: NO fork-sendable type-9 body can hit
the live record - p2-201/202's null was a client-local state miss (the slot's
setup state, not its identity). The designation arm is structurally closed;
type 9 joins the view on the never-send list. Full text + ENCODEDS (VMP
thunks and the member-resolver unreadable; the cookie-ring femu artifact
noted): RE_output/claims/session-identity-decode.md.

## 20.328 *** THE THREE-LANE SYNTHESIS: THE RECEIVER IS NOT REGISTERED BY ANY ***
## *** MESSAGE WE CAN SEND - BUT TYPE-51 IS NOW IMPLEMENTABLE, AND ITS "APPLY ***
## *** HALF" IS THE ONLY STARTUP-SEMANTIC LEVER LEFT. ***

R1 LANE A (session-identity-decode.md, 20.327): the type-9 body's session id is
stored-then-ignored; the slot is selected client-locally; the apply is a
state-machine STEP requiring the slot already in {active + established-member +
tracking-data} state. The state is created by the client's managed-session
setup, gated on the per-peer "activity-setup-complete" signal the fork does not
publish (ms-start-gate CLAIMs 6/7 - the member flag bytes at +0xED/+0xEF, and
the live server setting `member_setup_flags=0`).

R2 LANE C (type54-and-receiver-gate.md): the four ent_recv instance vtables
have ZERO instances in all four held dumps (two runtime bases) - the receive
blocks were never constructed, hard-confirmed. The chain is caller-verified end
to end: orchestrator 0x140B5ECD0 / job runner 0x1416CCDA0 -> sweep 0x1416F6640
(per-connection; gate [rcx+8]==1; entry [+0x70]==0 idle AND [+0x109]!=0 armed;
slots stride 0x11E08 at [rcx+0x178]) -> 0x14170980 0 -> the VMP gate byte
[0x14059DD80-result +0x25] -> ctor 0x1416BB1E0. The gate cluster is READABLE:
0x142037AF0=1 (master, armed), AF1/AF2/AF3=0, B08=1, B09=1. The sweep's own
conditions are ordinary heap state; the ONLY VMP link is the final byte.
Type-54's record format is VMP-unrecoverable (recipient registry 0x14281EDA0
NULL; zero non-empty 54 in any archive; our "6-bit host count" comment is
single-source and unaudited). VERDICT: the receive blocks are NOT registered by
any activity message the fork sends.

R3 LANE B (type51-bubble-startup-spec.md): type-51 (bubble_host_startup_info)
IS implementable. The wire body is SCHEMA-WALKED PROTOBUF (tag = field<<3|
wiretype; decoder FUN_140E74450; 5 fields: two 0x70-byte sub-messages, two
4-byte scalars, one 0x13F0 buffer). The validator (FUN_140BA61C0) contract at
the decoded-struct level: bytes +0x00/+0x78/+0xF8/+0x100 nonzero; u64
magics 0x56 @+0x10 and +0x88; then a FULL 0x56-byte memcmp of struct
[0x90..0xE6] against the client's OWN SteamNetworkingIdentity
`steamid:<id>#<token>` + 0-pad + version byte 0x06 (DAT_1426BDCC8 row 2,
dump-verified). THE TOKEN IS NOT A SECRET - it is the client's own published
identity (20.42 already captures it server-side); the fork ECHOES it. It is

R4 THE SYNTHESIS: no wire message registers the receive blocks (R2), and no
wire body can hit the type-9 step (R1). The one implementable message with a
STARTUP semantic is type-51, and its apply half (FUN_140B928D0) is the
